message.content:
I'd like us to rework the image generation vertical. There's a new model out today, `Qwen-Image-2.1`, which I've cloned into the models directory. We're going to reqwrite our goal for the vertical to rip out Z-Image-Turbo (for both generation and edits) and replace it with this model.

Here's some useful resources that will help:
  * Weights: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1
  * Blog post: https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1
  * Examples: https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1
  * Sample implementation: https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14804
  * Sample implementation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39983
    * There should be a tiny autoencoder that can preview this model here (TAEW2.1): https://github.com/madebyollin/taehv 

Your first task is to research this model, establish a plan for how we'll migrate to it (don't worry about breaking the vertical, that's fine), and write the plan in `./IMAGE.md` which we'll reuse in future sessions to get this done.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

- omarchy: REQUIRED for end-user customization of Linux desktop, window manager, or system config. Use when editing ~/.config/hypr/, ~/.config/waybar/, ~/.config/walker/, ~/.config/alacritty/, ~/.config/foot/, ~/.config/kitty/, ~/.config/ghostty/, ~/.config/mako/, or ~/.config/omarchy/. Triggers: Hyprland, window rules, animations, keybindings, monitors, gaps, borders, blur, opacity, waybar, walker, terminal config, themes, wallpaper, night light, idle, lock screen, screenshots, reminders, layer rules, workspace settings, display config, and user-facing omarchy commands. Excludes Omarchy source development in ~/.local/share/omarchy/ and `omarchy dev` workflows.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). 1	# Long Term Vision + Goal

# Long Term Vision + Goal

This project explores the most efficient ways to run a variety of AI/LLM generations on **Vulkan** using the AMD AI MAX+ 395 "Strix Halo" platform, with gfx1151 and RDNA3.5. 

Ultimately we want to be able to run these tasks:
  1. Speech to Text via Nvidia's `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`:
    * https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v2
  2. Text generation via Qwen's `Qwen3.8-Next-Flash`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30320v1
    * We'll need to quantise the weights once we've determined the most efficient method for the hardware
  3. Text to Speech via Hexgrad's `kokoro-82M`:
    * https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2306.07691v2
  4. Image generation via Tongyi's `z-image-turbo`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2511.22699v5
    * With this smaller model to generate in-progress previews: 
      * https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/taef1
  5. Compute embeddings via Qwen's `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05176v3

We will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these features, in Go.

41	purpose — so no footprint quantisation is planned for the small verticals.

43	---
44	
45	## Text generation (archive: [`research/llm-vertical.md`](research/llm-vertical.md), review: [`research/llm-review.md`](research/llm-review.md))
46	
47	**Where it stands.** Phases 1 and 2 are done on both axes and every P-stage
48	through P5 is closed. The shipped configuration is **D19 + D20 + D21**
49	(4.5-bit dense bank with a fifth bit on three families, the MoE rows
50	transcoded, `ffn_down_exps` at IQ4_NL): 4.132 GB a token against a 58.6
51	tok/s ceiling, perplexity 4.0992 (+1.74% of our own 4.0289, which is itself
52	−0.13% against llama.cpp's at identical weights). Decode 36.19 tok/s,
53	prefill 1089 tok/s at ubatch 2048. Served with prefix reuse; a second turn
54	extends the graph's state rather than re-prefilling.
55	
56	**Speculation (P5) is built, lossless, and parked at 0.95x.** The rollback
57	costs nothing when off. What would take it past 1.0, in order: the draft
58	head's **acceptance on a real workload** — 65.6% on prose against a
59	break-even of ~0.72; measure chat/code with the observer
60	(`cmd/llm -mtp`, ~3 min, no machinery) *before* building anything, and only
61	above a ≈ 0.8 does the rest get interesting — then the recovery round
62	(~0.95 → 1.05x) and pre-recording the verification pass (~2%). Hard
63	ceiling: speculation refuses past 2048 cells (`blk.48` has no compress
64	ratio). Narrowing the trunk makes speculation worse, twice — the draft
65	stages at checkpoint widths and acceptance falls as the trunk moves away
66	from what the draft predicts.
67	
68	**Open, in rough order of value:**
69	
70	- **P6 — batching.** Blocked on the product question: will the API serve
71	  more than one stream? Each sequence owns 113 MB of DeltaNet state plus
72	  rings and KV. P5b already built the first stage (R-row decode GEMVs,
73	  shipped at R = 2); raising `GEMVMaxRows` must land in the same commit as
74	  its rung in `TestGraphIsAChunkSplit` — R rows were correct in a block test
75	  and wrong in the model three separate ways (P5c).
76	- **Context depth is now the largest measured regression.** One-run figures
77	  from `cmd/llm -depth` (2026-09-19, shipped banks, no reproducibility pair
78	  yet): decode **24.27 → 3.98 tok/s between depth 0 and 64k — 6.1x — and it
79	  is all attention** (tg attention share 36.4% → 86.1%; MoE flat). Prefill
80	  halves. The QSA sparse selection does not stop it. And **128k does not
81	  complete**: the fill dies at ~115k cells in the P0 timestamp pathology
82	  ("N of 1025 timestamp slots never became ready"), reached by depth instead
83	  of row count — the untried route is making `DispatchMultiMarked`'s
84	  per-dispatch marks optional, since they are pure instrumentation. Needs a
85	  second run, then attribution of the attention growth (the 2051-cell read
86	  cap says the *selection* is not the term that grows).
87	- **Long-context gates** (idea 7, enabled by P0): perplexity at ctx 4096 is
88	  done (3.9392, −2.23% against ctx 2048 — the selection helps); a needle
89	  test through the API is not run.
90	- **The downstream task eval** — the last unpriced thing about the widths.
91	  At +1.74% of wikitext perplexity the instrument may no longer separate
92	  plans; a few hundred multiple-choice items through the HTTP API is an
93	  evening.
94	- **`Reset` is owed a test.** A fresh sequence is not independent of the one
95	  before it (P5c finding 6): three plain greedy runs over one prompt give
96	  three different texts, deterministically, when the previous run left cells
97	  past the new prompt's end. Any future token-for-token claim needs the
98	  plain-against-plain row printed beside it.
99	- **Priced and not taken** (in the archives, with numbers): the router's
100	  padding (+0.09 tok/s), re-screening the GEMV rungs at the q5 width, fp16
101	  DeltaNet state (+~1.3 ceiling), the unpack prefetch (~1.1x prefill), the
102	  asymmetric epilogue's GEMM arm, W4A8, the hot-expert fast path, the
103	  float-atomic combine, the vision tower. Also unexplained and written
104	  down: a dispatch is 8–22% slower inside a step than alone on a cold bank
105	  (P1b's 1.33 ms environment gap), and dispatch time is not a function of
106	  its bytes in either direction (P3a/P4b, opposite signs).
107	
108	**Instrument rules that must survive** (each earned the hard way): a
109	whole-model number needs a **same-hour control** (P1c — the machine moved
110	8.7 ms a step overnight); a ladder rate above 242 GB/s is an L3 hit, and
111	its *byte count* can lie too (D16, P4a); a plan is **measured, never
112	composed** (additivity leaks both ways through the n-gram block); a control
113	has to be able to fail (P5b shipped green tests on stale SPIR-V — `.comp`
114	edits need `go generate` before measuring); benchmarks need
115	`LLM_BANK_CACHE` set or a shipped-bank run re-fits for 8 minutes
116	(`cmd/serve` sets it, `cmd/llm` does not).
117	
118	## Speech → text (archive: [`research/speech-vertical.md`](research/speech-vertical.md))
119	
120	**Where it stands.** S1–S8 done: front end 21 ms + encoder 17 + decode 5 =
121	43 ms for jfk.wav, transcript exact, word/segment timings from the model's
122	own TDT durations, served at `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and over Wyoming
123	(with resampling at that door only).
124	
125	**Open:**
126	
127	- **S10 — the front end is 48% of the pipeline**: a few thousand 512-point
128	  float64 FFTs on the host. Either a float32 radix-4 on the host or the
129	  STFT + mel filterbank as two dispatches (the filterbank is a
130	  `[T, 257] x [257, 128]` GEMM; `kokoro_istft.comp` is the worked inverse).
131	- **The submit+fence is 38% of an emission** (40 µs of 105 per token). A
132	  persistent kernel — which is also what streaming transcripts would want —
133	  and/or speculating on blanks (consecutive-frame joints are independent
134	  during a blank run: one GEMM at M = 16 for the price of M = 1).
135	- **S9 — long clips.** Full attention means a chunk boundary changes every
136	  frame; chunking belongs in the design. The quadratic term arrives around
137	  1024 frames (~82 s); `-max-audio` refuses past the sizing today.
138	- Small: cache `UploadMel`'s sinusoidal position rows (1 ms, depends only
139	  on T); the eight per-head position-score GEMMs are §3.5's grouped shape.
140	
141	## Text → speech (archive: [`research/speech-vertical.md`](research/speech-vertical.md), recap: [`research/tts-recap.md`](research/tts-recap.md))
142	
143	**Where it stands.** T1–T10 and W1 done. Every stage on the device, staged
144	once for the life of the server (T9: the endpoint went 550 → 59 ms with
145	byte-identical audio); voices blend in upstream's own spelling (T8); T10
146	put PL-BERT's attention on the matrix cores so synthesis is a straight
147	8.0 ms per second of audio at every length. The round trip
148	(`cmd/roundtrip`) closes at 70.1x real time, six prose cases exact.
149	
150	**Open, in order of what a round trip buys:**
151	
152	- **The generator's 12 ms and the tail's 8** — the only arithmetic-bound
153	  parts of the model, 65% of a short utterance, measured since T4.
154	- **The host embedding stack** (R1's #2): `bert` is 12 ms of a paragraph
155	  and only 2.5 on the device — the "not worth a dispatch" comment is stale
156	  the same way the attention kernel's was.
157	- **Three boundaries, one change each**: the excitation's 0.2 ms is 88%
158	  submit+readback (move the two noise convolutions onto the device and
159	  nothing of that stage touches the bus); the phoneme side's remaining 6 ms
160	  is readbacks and submits (move the vocoder's input boundary); a 16 kHz
161	  path out of the vocoder would delete the client resample (9.7% of the
162	  loop — can the iSTFT head be asked for the rate directly?).
163	- **G2P on unseen text**: designed corpus 24/24; on 400 unseen sentences
164	  68.8% of sentences, 92.4% of phoneme words agree with misaki. Closing the
165	  gap is more *measured* rules — the syntactically obvious ones scored
166	  worse than no tagger.
167	- **Known, unsettled**: the style row is indexed by the phoneme *character*
168	  count (upstream's behaviour), so a front end emitting different characters
169	  picks a different row. And kokoro spells numbers out where parakeet writes
170	  digits back — the round trip measures those three cases and does not
171	  count them as failures.
172	
173	## Image generation (archive: [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md), slice: [`research/zimage-pipeline.md`](research/zimage-pipeline.md))
174	
175	**Where it stands.** The slice (stages 1–10) hit 14.26 s an image; serving
176	work closed 2026-09-18: variable geometry under a ceiling (I1), taef1
177	previews with `stream: true` (I2 — three partials cost 4.4% and put a
178	picture at 3.6 s), and `/v1/images/edits` over SDEdit with the ported VAE
179	encoder (I7 — an edit is cheaper than a generation by exactly the steps it
180	skips). Reproduces diffusers to 2.2e-2; every capability `GOALS.md` names
181	is served. Kernel work parked; the order was capabilities before percents,
182	and the capabilities ran out.
183	
184	**Open (all percents):**
185	
186	- **I3 + I5 + I8 + I9 — the same fusion in four places, 1.9 s of 14.3**: a
187	  bandwidth-bound elementwise pass whose consumer could absorb it (the
188	  DiT's eight passes 1.6 s, the VAE decoder's ~200 ms, taef1's pack 38 ms
189	  of an 87 ms preview, the encoder's group norms 128 ms of 425).
190	- **I4 — the GEMMs' missing quarter, 2.6 s** at 73–76% of the WMMA ceiling.
191	  No known lever; every measured one is applied.
192	- **I6 — attention's last 1.1x, ~0.2 s** — parked, register-bound, twice
193	  measured.
194	- The **~50 ms/step no dispatch accounts for** (per-dispatch timestamps —
195	  the L7d tool — would attribute it), and **hypothesis 5**: one kernel wins
196	  all three DiT shapes was measured at M=4096 only; variable size makes
197	  M=1152 real (`cmd/ditstack -image 1024`, `qwen.PlanFor` is the precedent).
198	- **Masked edits**: refused with a 501 that says what it would be. Nothing
199	  in `GOALS.md` asks for it.
200	
201	**Not planned**: quantisation (compute-bound at every servable size, §3.4;
202	int8 WMMA runs at fp16 rate, §0; and the two-machine deployment removes the
203	footprint argument). Sampling the encoder's posterior (breaks seed
204	reproducibility).
205	
206	## Embeddings (archive: [`research/embedding-vertical.md`](research/embedding-vertical.md))
207	
208	**Where it stands.** E0–E8 done except E7. Same `zimage/qwen` transformer,
209	third caller; 500 lines of package. A ≤32-token text costs what the weights
210	cost (11.5 ms, 32% of the bus); cosine 0.999999+ against fp32. Served with
211	MRL `dimensions` and the non-OpenAI `instruct` field.
212	
213	**Open: E7, batching — up to 10x on short texts.** The projections already
214	take M; the blocker is attention (two texts in one causal stream need a
215	block-diagonal mask). Measure the cheap shape first: **attention per
216	segment, projections batched** — attention is 1.5% of the graph and the
217	push block already carries per-text offsets, so no shader changes. The
218	segmented-mask kernel is the fallback. Quantisation stays unplanned until
219	a batch makes the weights the limit again.
220	
221	## The server, cross-vertical (docs: [`API.md`](API.md))
222	
223	- **Constrained decoding** — the one refusal that is a missing capability:
224	  would close `response_format`, `text.format` and named `tool_choice`.
225	- **More than one conversation** — the graph is one sequence's; two clients
226	  take turns evicting each other's prefix. A cache per conversation is a
227	  measurement (residency) plus P6's scheduler question.
228	- **The image adapter holds the device lock for the whole run** (the LLM's
229	  is per forward pass). Same fix shape; what a waiting speech request
230	  actually gains is a measurement.
231	- `n > 1` images are serial (capped at 4); a forced alignment for
232	  transcript timings if the 80 ms grid ever isn't enough.
233	
234	---
235	
236	## Where the old files went (2026-09-20 consolidation)
237	
238	| was | now |
239	|---|---|
240	| `LLM.md` | [`research/llm-vertical.md`](research/llm-vertical.md) — stages, decisions D1–D21, open questions, how-to-run |
241	| `LLM2.md` | [`research/llm-review.md`](research/llm-review.md) — hypotheses checked, decode budget, P0–P6 as closed |
242	| `SPEECH.md` | [`research/speech-vertical.md`](research/speech-vertical.md) — S1–S8, T1–T10, R1, W1 write-ups |
243	| `TTS.md` | [`research/tts-recap.md`](research/tts-recap.md) |
244	| `IMAGE.md` | [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md) |
245	| `PIPELINE.md` | [`research/zimage-pipeline.md`](research/zimage-pipeline.md) — inventory, validation rules, budget |
246	| `EMBEDDING.md` | [`research/embedding-vertical.md`](research/embedding-vertical.md) |
247	| `IDEAS.md` | [`research/ideas.md`](research/ideas.md) — the `§N.M` backlog and the measured roofline |
248	| `TODO.md` (session log) | distilled into `research/` as each stage closed; the phase-1 tail is [`research/phase1-backlog.md`](research/phase1-backlog.md); the full log is in git history |
249	
250	Per-experiment findings remain one file each in [`research/`](research/README.md),
251	indexed there. `§N.M` numbers are permanent addresses — never renumber.
252

  is all attention** (tg attention share 36.4% → 86.1%; MoE flat). Prefill
  halves. The QSA sparse selection does not stop it. And **128k does not
  complete**: the fill dies at ~115k cells in the P0 timestamp pathology
  ("N of 1025 timestamp slots never became ready"), reached by depth instead
  of row count — the untried route is making `DispatchMultiMarked`'s
  per-dispatch marks optional, since they are pure instrumentation. Needs a
  second run, then attribution of the attention growth (the 2051-cell read
  cap says the *selection* is not the term that grows).
- **Long-context gates** (idea 7, enabled by P0): perplexity at ctx 4096 is
  done (3.9392, −2.23% against ctx 2048 — the selection helps); a needle
  test through the API is not run.
- **The downstream task eval** — the last unpriced thing about the widths.
  At +1.74% of wikitext perplexity the instrument may no longer separate
  plans; a few hundred multiple-choice items through the HTTP API is an
  evening.
- **`Reset` is owed a test.** A fresh sequence is not independent of the one
  before it (P5c finding 6): three plain greedy runs over one prompt give
  three different texts, deterministically, when the previous run left cells
  past the new prompt's end. Any future token-for-token claim needs the
  plain-against-plain row printed beside it.
- **Priced and not taken** (in the archives, with numbers): the router's
  padding (+0.09 tok/s), re-screening the GEMV rungs at the q5 width, fp16
  DeltaNet state (+~1.3 ceiling), the unpack prefetch (~1.1x prefill), the
  asymmetric epilogue's GEMM arm, W4A8, the hot-expert fast path, the
  float-atomic combine, the vision tower. Also unexplained and written
  down: a dispatch is 8–22% slower inside a step than alone on a cold bank
  (P1b's 1.33 ms environment gap), and dispatch time is not a function of
  its bytes in either direction (P3a/P4b, opposite signs).

**Instrument rules that must survive** (each earned the hard way): a
whole-model number needs a **same-hour control** (P1c — the machine moved
8.7 ms a step overnight); a ladder rate above 242 GB/s is an L3 hit, and
its *byte count* can lie too (D16, P4a); a plan is **measured, never
composed** (additivity leaks both ways through the n-gram block); a control
has to be able to fail (P5b shipped green tests on stale SPIR-V — `.comp`
edits need `go generate` before measuring); benchmarks need
`LLM_BANK_CACHE` set or a shipped-bank run re-fits for 8 minutes
(`cmd/serve` sets it, `cmd/llm` does not).

## Speech → text (archive: [`research/speech-vertical.md`](research/speech-vertical.md))

**Where it stands.** S1–S8 done: front end 21 ms + encoder 17 + decode 5 =
43 ms for jfk.wav, transcript exact, word/segment timings from the model's
own TDT durations, served at `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and over Wyoming
(with resampling at that door only).

**Open:**

- **S10 — the front end is 48% of the pipeline**: a few thousand 512-point
  float64 FFTs on the host. Either a float32 radix-4 on the host or the
  STFT + mel filterbank as two dispatches (the filterbank is a
  `[T, 257] x [257, 128]` GEMM; `kokoro_istft.comp` is the worked inverse).
- **The submit+fence is 38% of an emission** (40 µs of 105 per token). A
  persistent kernel — which is also what streaming transcripts would want —
  and/or speculating on blanks (consecutive-frame joints are independent
  during a blank run: one GEMM at M = 16 for the price of M = 1).
- **S9 — long clips.** Full attention means a chunk boundary changes every
  frame; chunking belongs in the design. The quadratic term arrives around
  1024 frames (~82 s); `-max-audio` refuses past the sizing today.
- Small: cache `UploadMel`'s sinusoidal position rows (1 ms, depends only
  on T); the eight per-head position-score GEMMs are §3.5's grouped shape.

## Text → speech (archive: [`research/speech-vertical.md`](research/speech-vertical.md), recap: [`research/tts-recap.md`](research/tts-recap.md))

**Where it stands.** T1–T10 and W1 done. Every stage on the device, staged
once for the life of the server (T9: the endpoint went 550 → 59 ms with
byte-identical audio); voices blend in upstream's own spelling (T8); T10
put PL-BERT's attention on the matrix cores so synthesis is a straight
8.0 ms per second of audio at every length. The round trip
(`cmd/roundtrip`) closes at 70.1x real time, six prose cases exact.

**Open, in order of what a round trip buys:**

- **The generator's 12 ms and the tail's 8** — the only arithmetic-bound
  parts of the model, 65% of a short utterance, measured since T4.
- **The host embedding stack** (R1's #2): `bert` is 12 ms of a paragraph
  and only 2.5 on the device — the "not worth a dispatch" comment is stale
  the same way the attention kernel's was.
- **Three boundaries, one change each**: the excitation's 0.2 ms is 88%
  submit+readback (move the two noise convolutions onto the device and
  nothing of that stage touches the bus); the phoneme side's remaining 6 ms
  is readbacks and submits (move the vocoder's input boundary); a 16 kHz
  path out of the vocoder would delete the client resample (9.7% of the
  loop — can the iSTFT head be asked for the rate directly?).
- **G2P on unseen text**: designed corpus 24/24; on 400 unseen sentences
  68.8% of sentences, 92.4% of phoneme words agree with misaki. Closing the
  gap is more *measured* rules — the syntactically obvious ones scored
  worse than no tagger.
- **Known, unsettled**: the style row is indexed by the phoneme *character*
  count (upstream's behaviour), so a front end emitting different characters
  picks a different row. And kokoro spells numbers out where parakeet writes
  digits back — the round trip measures those three cases and does not
  count them as failures.

## Image generation (archive: [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md), slice: [`research/zimage-pipeline.md`](research/zimage-pipeline.md))

**Where it stands.** The slice (stages 1–10) hit 14.26 s an image; serving
work closed 2026-09-18: variable geometry under a ceiling (I1), taef1
previews with `stream: true` (I2 — three partials cost 4.4% and put a
picture at 3.6 s), and `/v1/images/edits` over SDEdit with the ported VAE
encoder (I7 — an edit is cheaper than a generation by exactly the steps it
skips). Reproduces diffusers to 2.2e-2; every capability `GOALS.md` names
is served. Kernel work parked; the order was capabilities before percents,
and the capabilities ran out.

**Open (all percents):**

- **I3 + I5 + I8 + I9 — the same fusion in four places, 1.9 s of 14.3**: a
  bandwidth-bound elementwise pass whose consumer could absorb it (the
  DiT's eight passes 1.6 s, the VAE decoder's ~200 ms, taef1's pack 38 ms
  of an 87 ms preview, the encoder's group norms 128 ms of 425).
- **I4 — the GEMMs' missing quarter, 2.6 s** at 73–76% of the WMMA ceiling.
  No known lever; every measured one is applied.
- **I6 — attention's last 1.1x, ~0.2 s** — parked, register-bound, twice
  measured.
- The **~50 ms/step no dispatch accounts for** (per-dispatch timestamps —
  the L7d tool — would attribute it), and **hypothesis 5**: one kernel wins
  all three DiT shapes was measured at M=4096 only; variable size makes
  M=1152 real (`cmd/ditstack -image 1024`, `qwen.PlanFor` is the precedent).
- **Masked edits**: refused with a 501 that says what it would be. Nothing
  in `GOALS.md` asks for it.

**Not planned**: quantisation (compute-bound at every servable size, §3.4;
int8 WMMA runs at fp16 rate, §0; and the two-machine deployment removes the
footprint argument). Sampling the encoder's posterior (breaks seed
reproducibility).

## Embeddings (archive: [`research/embedding-vertical.md`](research/embedding-vertical.md))

**Where it stands.** E0–E8 done except E7. Same `zimage/qwen` transformer,
third caller; 500 lines of package. A ≤32-token text costs what the weights
cost (11.5 ms, 32% of the bus); cosine 0.999999+ against fp32. Served with
MRL `dimensions` and the non-OpenAI `instruct` field.

**Open: E7, batching — up to 10x on short texts.** The projections already
take M; the blocker is attention (two texts in one causal stream need a
block-diagonal mask). Measure the cheap shape first: **attention per
segment, projections batched** — attention is 1.5% of the graph and the
push block already carries per-text offsets, so no shader changes. The
segmented-mask kernel is the fallback. Quantisation stays unplanned until
a batch makes the weights the limit again.

## The server, cross-vertical (docs: [`API.md`](API.md))

- **Constrained decoding** — the one refusal that is a missing capability:
  would close `response_format`, `text.format` and named `tool_choice`.
- **More than one conversation** — the graph is one sequence's; two clients
  take turns evicting each other's prefix. A cache per conversation is a
  measurement (residency) plus P6's scheduler question.
- **The image adapter holds the device lock for the whole run** (the LLM's
  is per forward pass). Same fix shape; what a waiting speech request
  actually gains is a measurement.
- `n > 1` images are serial (capped at 4); a forced alignment for
  transcript timings if the 80 ms grid ever isn't enough.

---

## Where the old files went (2026-09-20 consolidation)

| was | now |
|---|---|
| `LLM.md` | [`research/llm-vertical.md`](research/llm-vertical.md) — stages, decisions D1–D21, open questions, how-to-run |
| `LLM2.md` | [`research/llm-review.md`](research/llm-review.md) — hypotheses checked, decode budget, P0–P6 as closed |
| `SPEECH.md` | [`research/speech-vertical.md`](research/speech-vertical.md) — S1–S8, T1–T10, R1, W1 write-ups |
| `TTS.md` | [`research/tts-recap.md`](research/tts-recap.md) |
| `IMAGE.md` | [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md) |
| `PIPELINE.md` | [`research/zimage-pipeline.md`](research/zimage-pipeline.md) — inventory, validation rules, budget |
| `EMBEDDING.md` | [`research/embedding-vertical.md`](research/embedding-vertical.md) |
| `IDEAS.md` | [`research/ideas.md`](research/ideas.md) — the `§N.M` backlog and the measured roofline |
| `TODO.md` (session log) | distilled into `research/` as each stage closed; the phase-1 tail is [`research/phase1-backlog.md`](research/phase1-backlog.md); the full log is in git history |

Per-experiment findings remain one file each in [`research/`](research/README.md),
indexed there. `§N.M` numbers are permanent addresses — never renumber.

# Qwen-Image 2.1 Integration Summary

## Pipeline Architecture

The PR introduces `QwenImage21Pipeline` for unified text-to-image and image-conditioned generation. Key classes include:

- **QwenImage21Transformer2DModel**: A 7.1B single-stream transformer with block-causal attention and timestep-zero modulation for text and condition-image prefixes
- **AutoencoderKLQwenImage21**: A 64-channel VAE with 4 spatial downsamples (scale factor 16) and RGBA channel support
- **QwenImage21Pipeline**: Handles both generation modes through a single interface

## Transformer Design

The transformer employs block-causal attention where "the joint text/image sequence is causal while each image block stays internally bidirectional." This architecture is implemented via compiled `flex_attention` BlockMask for efficiency at high resolutions (2048×2048).

Two attention processors are available: `QwenImage21FlexAttnProcessor` (optimized, requires compilation) and `QwenImage21AttnProcessor` (default, works out-of-box).

## Text Encoding

The pipeline uses Qwen's text encoder, extracting pre-norm hidden states via a forward hook to maintain compatibility across transformer versions. Image markers follow the training template (`<image1>`, `<image2>`) and empty prompts become spaces.

## VAE & Image Handling

The VAE processes 4-channel RGBA images with alpha composited over white during encoding. Condition images are packed into the sequence, and a prefix KV cache mechanism caches text/condition embeddings from timestep zero, requiring recomputation only for target image tokens.

## Inference Defaults

The model recommends **40 denoising steps without classifier-free guidance** (`true_cfg_scale=1.0`), differing from other Qwen-Image variants that use 50 steps with guidance scale 4.0.

# Qwen-Image-2.1 Repository Summary

## Core Capabilities

**Text-to-Image Generation**: The model creates images from text prompts at native 2K resolution (2048×2048).

**Image Editing**: Supports single and multi-image editing with up to 10 reference images for composition tasks. Enables local edits via circles, painted annotations, or separate masks.

**Native Transparency**: Generates RGBA images with transparent backgrounds using the prompt format: "This is an RGBA image with transparency. <description>. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent."

## Architecture

The model features a "single-stream DiT with 32 layers" and 7B parameters in its visual generation component. It uses "block-causal attention" where tokens attend based on position or image block relationships. A Qwen3-VL 8B vision-language model encodes both text instructions and condition images into unified representations for the VAE decoder.

The design includes "mixed-granularity attention architecture" enabling "prefix KV cache reuse"—input images and text are computed once at the first denoising step and cached across subsequent steps, improving efficiency for editing tasks.

## Recommended Settings

- **Inference steps**: 40 (default)
- **Guidance scale**: 1 (mentioned in examples)
- **Resolution**: 2048×2048 standard, with supported aspect ratios (1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 16:9, etc.)
- **Scheduler**: Flow Matching with Euler discrete scheduling

## Integration & Support

Multiple inference frameworks offer optimized implementations: Diffusers (recommended via `QwenImage21Pipeline`), vLLM-Omni, SGLang-Diffusion, ComfyUI, and LightX2V. Prompt rewriting models (T2I and I2I variants) are available as separate checkpoints.

# Qwen-Image-2.1 Implementation in SGLang

## DiT Architecture

The PR implements native Qwen-Image 2.1 support with a custom DiT (Diffusion Transformer) component. The implementation preserves "Transformers 4.57.3 conditioning semantics" while integrating advanced optimization techniques including complex RoPE, Q/K normalization, and scale-only LayerNorm fusions.

## Attention & Caching Strategy

The implementation features block-causal attention with request-scoped prefix caching and "Cache-DiT" technology. The system maintains per-layer prefix KV cache structures, enabling efficient reuse across sequential requests while supporting breakable CUDA graphs for flexible scheduling.

## Text Encoding

Text conditioning relies on Qwen3-VL encoding with specific handling of hidden states. The PR aligns with "pre-final-norm text features" and implements proper "empty-prompt handling," ensuring consistent behavior across generation scenarios.

## Image Processing

Reference and edit images undergo dual-path processing:
- **VAE encoding**: Images compress to latent representations with RGBA support
- **Vision encoder**: Processes images through Qwen vision components with native encoder sharding

The implementation handles "white alpha compositing for vision only" and supports transparent image I/O.

## Performance Improvements

On B200 hardware, Q/K normalization reduced latency by 9.17% for generation (3.114→2.828s) and 7.81% for editing, with LayerNorm optimizations providing additional 2-3% gains while maintaining pixel-perfect output consistency.

# TAEHV: Tiny AutoEncoder for Video Models

## Overview
TAEHV is a lightweight video autoencoder designed for fast encoding/decoding of video latents across multiple generative models. It trades some quality for significant speed and memory improvements compared to full-size VAEs.

## Supported Models
TAEHV provides specialized weight files for:
- **Hunyuan Video** (v1, v1.5, v1.5_super variants)
- **Wan 2.1 & 2.2** (taew2_1, taew2_2, taew2_2_super)
- **Qwen Image** (uses taew2_1 weights)
- **MiniMax H3** (taeh3)
- **CogVideoX** (taecvx)
- **LTX-2 & LTX-2.3** (taeltx_2, taeltx2_3)
- **Open-Sora 1.3** (taeos1_3)

## Key Performance Metrics
The tool achieves approximately **0.5 seconds** for decoding 61 frames at 512×320 resolution with "less than 0.5GB" memory usage, versus 2-3 seconds and 6-9GB for full VAEs.

## Usage for Preview Decoding
Load weights by filename (e.g., `taew2_1.pth`), then call `decode_video()` on latents. Optional parameters allow disabling temporal or spatial upscaling for even faster preview generation. The `StreamingTAEHV` wrapper enables real-time processing for live video scenarios.

## Architecture Details
TAEHV maintains "NTCHW dimension order" (frames first) and stores images in the [0,1] range without applying latent scaling—directly compatible with diffusion model outputs. Input/output channel counts vary by variant but align with their respective base VAEs.

## File Naming Convention
Weight files follow patterns like `taew2_1.pth` and `taew2_1_super.pth`, with safetensors conversions available in the `/safetensors` subdirectory.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Qwen-Image-2.1:

## Architecture Overview

Qwen-Image-2.1 has a 7B parameters visual generation component built with 32 Single-Stream DiT layers. It uses a Qwen3-VL 8B text encoder and a 64-channel RGBA VAE at 16× spatial compression.

## Key Architectural Features

The model features a lightweight architecture with mixed-granularity attention and prefix KV cache reuse that delivers strong image quality at low computational cost. 

It uses block-causal attention with a token-level causal mask for text and a chunk-level bidirectional mask for image generation, plus prefix KV cache reuse for multi-image editing.

## Technical Details

The prefix KV cache implementation is sophisticated: The model's prefix KV is per layer, and each block keeps a stable _layer_id and slices prefix_caches itself.

## Image Generation Capabilities

The model supports native 2K resolution, defaulting to 2048×2048 at 40 steps, with seven aspect-ratio presets.

The search results focus primarily on technical documentation and implementation details from repositories like Hugging Face and GitHub rather than a dedicated blog post, but they provide comprehensive architectural information about the model.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the tiny autoencoder for Qwen-Image-2.1 with preview capabilities:

## Overview

QwenImage decodes Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-Edit latents — the Wan 2.1 VAE's 16-channel latent — with a pure-MLX port of madebyollin's taew2.1 tiny autoencoder.

## Architecture Details

The taew2.1 is a 2D-conv autoencoder with recurrent temporal blocks, run here for a single still image, and is the first variant on the new taehv architecture. Note that this is distinct from the standard 64-channel architecture mentioned in your query—the Wan 2.1/Qwen-Image VAE uses a **16-channel latent** space.

## Key Features

These are distilled mini-autoencoders that decode diffusion latents to RGB in milliseconds using a few-MB model instead of multi-GB full VAEs. It decodes a latent to an image about fifty times cheaper than the full VAE, which is what makes per-step previews affordable.

## Implementation

You can construct it with QwenImage.from_pretrained() for standalone decode/encode, or preview a live generation with LivePreviewCallback(variant="qwen-image"). This is available in the mlx-taef library, which provides MLX implementations of the TAESD family of tiny autoencoders.

# IMAGE — the z-image-turbo vertical

> **ARCHIVED 2026-09-20** — frozen as the closing record of the z-image-turbo vertical (I0–I7): serving, previews, edits, the re-checked hypotheses. It was
> `IMAGE.md` at the repo root; the live state of play is now [`../TODO.md`](../TODO.md).

> **Rewritten 2026-09-18 (I7), and this is the file to read first for this
> vertical.**
> It supersedes [`zimage-pipeline.md`](zimage-pipeline.md), which carries a banner saying so
> and whose stage table (1-10) and validation rules remain the record of how
> the slice was built. Same rules as `llm-vertical.md`, `speech-vertical.md` and `embedding-vertical.md`:
> this file is **rewritten** each session rather than appended to, history goes
> to `../TODO.md`, closed findings to `research/`. Stage numbers are **I0, I1, …**
> — the original slice's stages 1-10 keep their bare numbers in
> `stage-*.md` — and `§N.M` still addresses `ideas.md`.

**Target**: `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo` — prompt → PNG at up to 1024x1024, 8
steps, fp16, end to end in Go on Vulkan, served at
`POST /v1/images/generations`, with in-progress previews from
`madebyollin/taef1`.

**Status**: **every capability `../GOALS.md` names for this vertical is built and
served, and `../API.md` now carries no refusal that a flag does not fix.** The
kernel work was parked 2026-09-14 with the budget below; the serving work
unparked 2026-09-18. **I1** made width and height a *ceiling and a default
rather than a fixed size* and wired `/v1/images/generations`. **I2** ported
taef1 and turned on streaming. **I7** ported the VAE's **encoder** and wired
`/v1/images/edits` over SDEdit: a 1024x1024 edit is **11.3 s** against a
generation's 14.3, and it reproduces diffusers to **1.1e-2**. What is left is
four percentage items and one capability nobody has asked for (masks).

## Where the work stands

| # | Stage | State |
|---|---|---|
| I0 | The slice: stages 1-10, prompt → PNG in **14.26 s** | **done** — `zimage-pipeline.md`, `stage-*.md` |
| I1 | Served: variable geometry + `/v1/images/generations` | **done 2026-09-18** — `../API.md` carries the row and the flags |
| I2 | taef1 previews, and `stream: true` | **done 2026-09-18** — measured below |
| I7 | `/v1/images/edits`: the VAE encoder, and SDEdit | **done 2026-09-18** — `i7-vae-encoder-and-edits.md` |
| I3 | The eight elementwise passes, 1.6 s, fused into their GEMMs | open — the L2c/L2f pattern, proven since parking |
| I4 | The GEMMs' missing quarter, 2.6 s | open — two new probes since parking, no known lever |
| I5 | The VAE decoder's elementwise fusions, ~200 ms | open |
| I6 | Attention's last 1.1x, ~0.2 s | parked — register-bound, twice measured |
| I8 | taef1's pack pass, **38 ms of an 87 ms preview** | open |
| I9 | The **encoder's** group norms, **128 ms of a 425 ms encode** | open, and new — see I7 |

The order was **capabilities before percents**, and with I7 done it has run
out of capabilities: everything left is a percentage, except masked edits,
which nothing asked for. I3, I5, I8 and I9 are now visibly *the same item in
four shapes* — a bandwidth-bound elementwise pass that its consumer could
absorb — and together they are 1.9 s of the 14.3.

## The model, as the checkpoint describes it

`go run ./cmd/inspect models/Z-Image-Turbo/<part>`; full table in
`zimage-pipeline.md`. What the open items rest on:

204	            vae_scale_factor=self.vae_scale_factor, vae_latent_channels=self.latent_channels

206	        self.sys_prompt = "Comprehend and analyze the provided prompt."
207	        # The prompt is built as a raw template string and passed straight to
208	        # `self.processor(text=..., images=...)`, rather than going through `apply_chat_template`:
209	        # the two tokenize differently and the checkpoint expects this one. The "Picture 1: ..."
210	        # vision prefix only appears in the image-conditioned template.
211	        self.prompt_template_t2i = (
212	            f"<|im_start|>system\n{self.sys_prompt}<|im_end|>\n"
213	            f"<|im_start|>user\n{{}}<|im_end|>\n"
214	            f"<|im_start|>assistant\n"
215	        )
216	        self.prompt_template_ti2i = (
217	            f"<|im_start|>system\n{self.sys_prompt}<|im_end|>\n"
218	            f"<|im_start|>user\n<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>{{}}<|im_end|>\n"
219	            f"<|im_start|>assistant\n"
220	        )
221	        # Number of leading system-role tokens to drop from the hidden states. Derived from the
222	        # tokenized system message rather than hardcoded, so it tracks the processor's template.
223	        sys_message = [{"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": self.sys_prompt}]}]
224	        sys_tokens = self.processor.apply_chat_template(sys_message, tokenize=True, return_dict=False)
225	        self._drop_idx = len(sys_tokens[0])
226	        self._img_token_id = self.processor.tokenizer.encode("<|image_pad|>")[0]
227	
228	    def _extract_masked_hidden(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor):
229	        bool_mask = mask.bool()
230	        valid_lengths = bool_mask.sum(dim=1)
231	        selected = hidden_states[bool_mask]
232	        return torch.split(selected, valid_lengths.tolist(), dim=0)

234	    def _get_qwen_prompt_embeds(
235	        self,
236	        prompt: str | list[str] = None,
237	        image: list | None = None,
238	        device: torch.device | None = None,
239	    ):
240	        device = device or self._execution_device
241	        prompt = [prompt] if isinstance(prompt, str) else prompt
242	        # Qwen has no bos token, so an empty string leaves the encoder with nothing to read.
243	        prompt = [" " if not p else p for p in prompt]
244	        is_t2i = image is None
245	
246	        if is_t2i:
247	            prompts = [self.prompt_template_t2i.format(t) for t in prompt]
248	        else:
249	            prompts = []
250	            condition_pil_list = []
251	            for t in prompt:
252	                n_imgs = len(image)
253	                replace = "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>"
254	                for i in range(2, n_imgs + 1):
255	                    replace += f" <image{i}><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>"
256	                template = self.prompt_template_ti2i.replace(
257	                    "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>", replace
258	                )
259	                prompts.append(template.format(t))
260	            # Each prompt's template repeats the `<|image_pad|>` placeholders, so hand the processor one set of
261	            # images per prompt, in the order the placeholders appear.
262	            for _ in prompt:
263	                for img in image:
264	                    if not isinstance(img, PILImage.Image):
265	                        img = PILImage.fromarray(img)
266	                    if img.mode == "RGBA":
267	                        # The checkpoint was trained with the alpha composited over white for the vision encoder.
268	                        # Only this copy is flattened; the VAE still reads all four channels.
269	                        white = PILImage.new("RGB", img.size, (255, 255, 255))
270	                        white.paste(img, mask=img.getchannel("A"))
271	                        img = white
272	                    condition_pil_list.append(img)
273	
274	        # Left padding, as the checkpoint was trained with. `_extract_masked_hidden` drops the padding either way,
275	        # but the side decides the positions the encoder sees for a batch of prompts of different lengths.
276	        processor_kwargs = {
277	            "text": prompts,
278	            "padding": True,
279	            "padding_side": "left",
280	            "return_tensors": "pt",
281	        }
282	        if not is_t2i:
283	            processor_kwargs["images"] = condition_pil_list
284	
285	        model_inputs = self.processor(**processor_kwargs).to(device)
286	
287	        forward_kwargs = {
288	            "input_ids": model_inputs.input_ids,
289	            "attention_mask": model_inputs.attention_mask,
290	            "output_hidden_states": True,
291	        }
292	        if not is_t2i and hasattr(model_inputs, "pixel_values"):
293	            forward_kwargs.update(pixel_values=model_inputs.pixel_values, image_grid_thw=model_inputs.image_grid_thw)
294	        if hasattr(model_inputs, "mm_token_type_ids"):
295	            forward_kwargs["mm_token_type_ids"] = model_inputs.mm_token_type_ids
296	
297	        # `hidden_states[-1]` has to be the last decoder layer's output, before the text encoder's final RMSNorm:
298	        # that is what the transformer was trained on. It is what transformers 4.x returns there, but from
299	        # transformers 5.0 the output capturing ties that entry to `last_hidden_state`, so it comes back normalized
300	        # instead — a third of the signal the transformer reads, which shows up first in rendered text. A forward hook
301	        # returning the module's input replaces its output, which neutralizes the norm for this call on either version.
302	        # TODO: replace this with `tie_last_hidden_states=False` in the text encoder's config, which
303	        # huggingface/transformers#48087 adds, once that ships in a stable transformers release (5.18).
304	        text_model = getattr(self.text_encoder.model, "language_model", self.text_encoder.model)
305	        handle = text_model.norm.register_forward_hook(lambda module, args, output: args[0])
306	        try:
307	            outputs = self.text_encoder(**forward_kwargs)
308	        finally:
309	            handle.remove()
310	        hidden_states = outputs.hidden_states[-1]
311	
312	        split_hidden_states = list(self._extract_masked_hidden(hidden_states, model_inputs.attention_mask))
313	        split_hidden_states = [e[self._drop_idx :] for e in split_hidden_states]
314	
315	        image_pad_mask = [
316	            (sample_ids[sample_mask.bool()] == self._img_token_id)
317	            for sample_ids, sample_mask in zip(model_inputs.input_ids, model_inputs.attention_mask)
318	        ]
319	        image_pad_mask = [e[self._drop_idx :] for e in image_pad_mask]
320	
321	        attn_mask_list = [torch.ones(e.size(0), dtype=torch.long, device=e.device) for e in split_hidden_states]
322	        max_seq_len = max(e.size(0) for e in split_hidden_states)
323	        prompt_embeds = torch.stack(
324	            [torch.cat([u, u.new_zeros(max_seq_len - u.size(0), u.size(1))]) for u in split_hidden_states]
325	        )
326	        encoder_attention_mask = torch.stack(
327	            [torch.cat([u, u.new_zeros(max_seq_len - u.size(0))]) for u in attn_mask_list]
328	        )
329	        image_pad_mask = torch.stack([torch.cat([u, u.new_zeros(max_seq_len - u.size(0))]) for u in image_pad_mask])
330	
331	        return prompt_embeds, encoder_attention_mask, image_pad_mask
332	
333	    def encode_prompt(
334	        self,
335	        prompt: str | list[str],
336	        image: list[PipelineImageInput] | None = None,
337	        device: torch.device | None = None,
338	        num_images_per_prompt: int = 1,
339	        prompt_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
340	        prompt_embeds_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
341	        image_pad_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
342	    ):
343	        r"""
344	        Args:
345	            prompt (`str` or `list[str]`, *optional*):
346	                Prompt to be encoded.
347	            image (`list[PipelineImageInput]`, *optional*):
348	                Condition images to encode alongside the prompt.
349	            device (`torch.device`):
350	                Torch device.
351	            num_images_per_prompt (`int`):
352	                Number of images generated per prompt.
353	            prompt_embeds (`torch.Tensor`, *optional*):
354	                Pre-generated text embeddings. Skips encoding when provided.
355	        """
356	        device = device or self._execution_device
357	
358	        prompt = [prompt] if isinstance(prompt, str) else prompt
359	        batch_size = len(prompt) if prompt_embeds is None else prompt_embeds.shape[0]
360	
361	        if prompt_embeds is None:
362	            prompt_embeds, prompt_embeds_mask, image_pad_mask = self._get_qwen_prompt_embeds(prompt, image, device)
363	        elif image_pad_mask is None:
364	            if image is not None:
365	                raise ValueError(
366	                    "Pass `image_pad_mask` alongside `prompt_embeds` when the embeddings cover condition images, so "
367	                    "the transformer knows which positions hold image tokens."
368	                )
369	            # Embeddings supplied without a mask can only be text, so no position holds an image token.
370	            image_pad_mask = prompt_embeds.new_zeros(prompt_embeds.shape[:2], dtype=torch.bool)
371	
372	        _, seq_len, _ = prompt_embeds.shape
373	        prompt_embeds = prompt_embeds.repeat(1, num_images_per_prompt, 1)
374	        prompt_embeds = prompt_embeds.view(batch_size * num_images_per_prompt, seq_len, -1)
375	        # `repeat(1, n)` on the 2D mask, so its rows interleave the same way the 3D embeddings' do. With
376	        # `repeat(1, n, 1)` the mask picks up a leading axis and the rows come out tiled instead, which pairs each
377	        # sample with another prompt's padding.
378	        if prompt_embeds_mask is not None:
379	            prompt_embeds_mask = prompt_embeds_mask.repeat(1, num_images_per_prompt)
380	            prompt_embeds_mask = prompt_embeds_mask.view(batch_size * num_images_per_prompt, seq_len)
381	
382	        # Without padding there is nothing to mask, and a mask that carries no information costs the attention
383	        # backends that reject one outright.
384	        if prompt_embeds_mask is not None and prompt_embeds_mask.all():
385	            prompt_embeds_mask = None
386	
387	        return prompt_embeds, prompt_embeds_mask, image_pad_mask
388	
389	    def check_inputs(self, prompt, height, width, prompt_embeds, callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs):
390	        if height % (self.vae_scale_factor * 2) != 0 or width % (self.vae_scale_factor * 2) != 0:
391	            logger.warning(
392	                f"`height` and `width` have to be divisible by {self.vae_scale_factor * 2} but are {height} and "
393	                f"{width}. Dimensions will be resized accordingly"
394	            )
395	
396	        if callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs is not None and not all(
397	            k in self._callback_tensor_inputs for k in callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs
398	        ):
399	            raise ValueError(
400	                f"`callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs` has to be in {self._callback_tensor_inputs}, but found "
401	                f"{[k for k in callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs if k not in self._callback_tensor_inputs]}"
402	            )
403	
404	        if prompt is not None and prompt_embeds is not None:
405	            raise ValueError("Pass either `prompt` or `prompt_embeds`, not both.")
406	        if prompt is None and prompt_embeds is None:
407	            raise ValueError("Pass one of `prompt` or `prompt_embeds`.")

409	    @staticmethod
410	    def _pack_latents(latents, batch_size, num_channels_latents, height, width):
411	        # 2.1 consumes latents unpatched, so packing is a plain spatial flatten.
412	        return latents.view(batch_size, num_channels_latents, height * width).transpose(1, 2)
413	
414	    @staticmethod
415	    def _unpack_latents(latents, height, width, vae_scale_factor):
416	        batch_size, _, channels = latents.shape
417	        height = 2 * (int(height) // (vae_scale_factor * 2))
418	        width = 2 * (int(width) // (vae_scale_factor * 2))
419	        latents = latents.transpose(1, 2).reshape(batch_size, channels, 1, height, width)
420	        return latents

422	    # Copied from diffusers.pipelines.qwenimage.pipeline_qwenimage_edit.QwenImageEditPipeline._encode_vae_image
423	    def _encode_vae_image(self, image: torch.Tensor, generator: torch.Generator):
424	        if isinstance(generator, list):
425	            image_latents = [
426	                retrieve_latents(self.vae.encode(image[i : i + 1]), generator=generator[i], sample_mode="argmax")
427	                for i in range(image.shape[0])
428	            ]
429	            image_latents = torch.cat(image_latents, dim=0)
430	        else:
431	            image_latents = retrieve_latents(self.vae.encode(image), generator=generator, sample_mode="argmax")
432	        latents_mean = (
433	            torch.tensor(self.vae.config.latents_mean)
434	            .view(1, self.latent_channels, 1, 1, 1)
435	            .to(image_latents.device, image_latents.dtype)
436	        )
437	        latents_std = (
438	            torch.tensor(self.vae.config.latents_std)
439	            .view(1, self.latent_channels, 1, 1, 1)
440	            .to(image_latents.device, image_latents.dtype)
441	        )
442	        image_latents = (image_latents - latents_mean) / latents_std
443	
444	        return image_latents

446	    def prepare_latents(
447	        self, images, batch_size, num_channels_latents, height, width, dtype, device, generator, latents=None
448	    ):
449	        height = 2 * (int(height) // (self.vae_scale_factor * 2))
450	        width = 2 * (int(width) // (self.vae_scale_factor * 2))
451	
452	        if isinstance(generator, list) and len(generator) != batch_size:
453	            raise ValueError(
454	                f"You have passed a list of generators of length {len(generator)}, but requested an effective batch"
455	                f" size of {batch_size}. Make sure the batch size matches the length of the generators."
456	            )
457	
458	        image_latents = None
459	        if images is not None:
460	            all_image_latents = []
461	            for image in images:
462	                image = image.to(device=device, dtype=dtype)
463	                encoded = self._encode_vae_image(image, generator)
464	                if batch_size > encoded.shape[0]:
465	                    if batch_size % encoded.shape[0] != 0:
466	                        raise ValueError(
467	                            f"Cannot duplicate `image` of batch size {encoded.shape[0]} to {batch_size} text prompts."
468	                        )
469	                    encoded = torch.cat([encoded] * (batch_size // encoded.shape[0]), dim=0)
470	                image_latent_height, image_latent_width = encoded.shape[3:]
471	                all_image_latents.append(
472	                    self._pack_latents(
473	                        encoded, batch_size, num_channels_latents, image_latent_height, image_latent_width
474	                    )
475	                )
476	            image_latents = torch.cat(all_image_latents, dim=1)
477	
478	        if latents is None:
479	            shape = (batch_size, 1, num_channels_latents, height, width)
480	            latents = randn_tensor(shape, generator=generator, device=device, dtype=dtype)
481	            latents = self._pack_latents(latents, batch_size, num_channels_latents, height, width)
482	        else:
483	            latents = latents.to(device=device, dtype=dtype)
484	
485	        return latents, image_latents

505	    def __call__(
506	        self,
507	        prompt: str | list[str] = None,
508	        image: PipelineImageInput | None = None,
509	        negative_prompt: str | list[str] = None,
510	        true_cfg_scale: float = 1.0,
511	        height: int | None = None,
512	        width: int | None = None,
513	        num_inference_steps: int = 40,
514	        sigmas: list[float] | None = None,
515	        num_images_per_prompt: int = 1,
516	        generator: torch.Generator | list[torch.Generator] | None = None,
517	        latents: torch.Tensor | None = None,
518	        prompt_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
519	        prompt_embeds_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
520	        negative_prompt_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
521	        negative_prompt_embeds_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
522	        output_type: str | None = "pil",
523	        return_dict: bool = True,
524	        attention_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
525	        callback_on_step_end: Callable[[int, int, dict], None] | None = None,
526	        callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs: list[str] = ["latents"],
527	        output_resolution: int = 1024,
528	        use_kv_cache: bool = True,
529	    ):
530	        r"""
531	        Function invoked when calling the pipeline for generation.
532	
533	        Args:
534	            prompt (`str` or `list[str]`, *optional*):
535	                The prompt to guide image generation. Pass `prompt_embeds` instead to supply embeddings directly.
536	            image (`PipelineImageInput`, *optional*):
537	                One or more condition images, as a PIL image or a numpy array. They are encoded by the text encoder as
538	                vision context and by the VAE into latent tokens prepended to the noise. A list is one set of images
539	                shared by every prompt in the batch, not one entry per prompt.
540	            negative_prompt (`str` or `list[str]`, *optional*):
541	                The prompt not to guide image generation. Ignored when `true_cfg_scale` is not greater than 1.
542	            true_cfg_scale (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 1.0):
543	                Classifier-free guidance scale. Enabled by `true_cfg_scale > 1` together with a negative prompt.
544	                Qwen-Image 2.1 is meant to be sampled without guidance, hence the default of 1.0.
545	            height (`int`, *optional*):
546	                Height in pixels of the generated image. Derived from the condition image's aspect ratio if omitted.
547	            width (`int`, *optional*):
548	                Width in pixels of the generated image. Derived from the condition image's aspect ratio if omitted.
549	            num_inference_steps (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 40):
550	                Number of denoising steps.
551	            sigmas (`list[float]`, *optional*):
552	                Custom sigmas for the denoising schedule.
553	            num_images_per_prompt (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 1):
554	                Number of images generated per prompt.
555	            generator (`torch.Generator` or `list[torch.Generator]`, *optional*):
556	                Generator(s) to make generation deterministic.
557	            latents (`torch.Tensor`, *optional*):
558	                Pre-generated noisy latents.
559	            prompt_embeds (`torch.Tensor`, *optional*):
560	                Pre-generated text embeddings, which skip prompt encoding. Pass `prompt_embeds_mask` with them.
561	            prompt_embeds_mask (`torch.Tensor`, *optional*):
562	                Bool mask marking the valid positions of `prompt_embeds`.
563	            negative_prompt_embeds (`torch.Tensor`, *optional*):
564	                Pre-generated negative text embeddings, used in place of `negative_prompt`. Pass
565	                `negative_prompt_embeds_mask` with them.
566	            negative_prompt_embeds_mask (`torch.Tensor`, *optional*):
567	                Bool mask marking the valid positions of `negative_prompt_embeds`.
568	            output_type (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"pil"`):
569	                Output format, `"pil"`, `"np"`, `"pt"` or `"latent"`.
570	            return_dict (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
571	                Whether to return a [`~pipelines.qwenimage.QwenImagePipelineOutput`] instead of a plain tuple.
572	            attention_kwargs (`dict`, *optional*):
573	                Passed through to the attention processor.
574	            callback_on_step_end (`Callable`, *optional*):
575	                Called at the end of each denoising step.
576	            callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs (`list[str]`, *optional*, defaults to `["latents"]`):
577	                Tensors from the denoising loop to hand to `callback_on_step_end`. They must be listed in the
578	                pipeline's `_callback_tensor_inputs`.
579	            output_resolution (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 1024):
580	                Target side length used to derive `height`/`width` and to resize condition images.
581	            use_kv_cache (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
582	                Cache the text and condition-image keys and values after the first step. Valid because
583	                `causal_condition` modulates those tokens from `t = 0`, making their activations step-independent.
584	
585	                Toggling this does not reproduce the same image bit-for-bit in reduced precision. Caching makes the
586	                decode step attend with a different sequence layout than the prefill step, so the two tile differently
587	                and land on different rounding; both agree with an fp32 reference to the same tolerance. A one-ULP
588	                difference at the first block is then amplified by 32 blocks and every sampler step, so the two
589	                settings give equally valid but visibly distinct samples. Fix a sample by fixing this flag.
590	
591	        Examples:
592	
593	        Returns:
594	            [`~pipelines.qwenimage.QwenImagePipelineOutput`] or `tuple`:
595	            [`~pipelines.qwenimage.QwenImagePipelineOutput`] if `return_dict` is True, otherwise a `tuple` whose first
596	            element is a list with the generated images.
597	        """
598	        if image is not None:
599	            # The text encoder reads each condition image as vision context, so the pixels have to be there. Normalize
600	            # to PIL up front, and everything downstream — the aspect ratio below, the resize, the VAE — sees one type.
601	            image = image if isinstance(image, list) else [image]
602	            condition_images = []
603	            for img in image:
604	                if isinstance(img, PILImage.Image):
605	                    condition_images.append(img)
606	                elif isinstance(img, np.ndarray):
607	                    condition_images.append(PILImage.fromarray(img))
608	                elif isinstance(img, (list, tuple)):
609	                    raise ValueError(
610	                        "`image` is one flat set of condition images that applies to every prompt in the batch, so it "
611	                        "cannot be nested per prompt. Call the pipeline once per prompt when they need different "
612	                        "condition images."
613	                    )
614	                else:
615	                    raise ValueError(
616	                        f"`image` accepts a PIL image or a numpy array, or a list of either, but got "
617	                        f"{type(img).__name__}. Latents cannot stand in for a condition image here, because the text "
618	                        f"encoder has to see the image itself."
619	                    )
620	            image = condition_images
621	            calculated_width, calculated_height, _ = calculate_dimensions(
622	                output_resolution * output_resolution, image[-1].size[0] / image[-1].size[1]
623	            )
624	            height = height or calculated_height
625	            width = width or calculated_width
626	        height = height or output_resolution
627	        width = width or output_resolution
628	
629	        self.check_inputs(prompt, height, width, prompt_embeds, callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs)
630	
631	        multiple_of = self.vae_scale_factor * 2
632	        width = width // multiple_of * multiple_of
633	        height = height // multiple_of * multiple_of
634	
635	        self._attention_kwargs = attention_kwargs or {}
636	        self._current_timestep = None
637	        self._interrupt = False
638	
639	        if prompt is not None and isinstance(prompt, str):
640	            batch_size = 1
641	        elif prompt is not None:
642	            batch_size = len(prompt)
643	        else:
644	            batch_size = prompt_embeds.shape[0]
645	
646	        device = self._execution_device
647	
648	        # 1. Preprocess condition images: one resize feeds both the text encoder and the VAE.
649	        input_image_sizes, input_images, vae_images = [], None, None
650	        if image is not None:
651	            input_images, vae_images = [], []
652	            for img in image:
653	                if hasattr(img, "mode") and img.mode != "RGBA":
654	                    img = img.convert("RGBA")
655	                image_width, image_height = img.size
656	                input_width, input_height, _ = calculate_dimensions(
657	                    output_resolution * output_resolution, image_width / image_height
658	                )
659	                input_image_sizes.append((input_width, input_height))
660	                input_images.append(self.image_processor.resize(img, width=input_width, height=input_height))
661	                vae_images.append(
662	                    self.image_processor.preprocess(img, width=input_width, height=input_height).unsqueeze(2)
663	                )
664	
665	        # 2. Encode prompt
666	        # The mask is not part of the condition: `encode_prompt` returns `None` for it when nothing is padded, so
667	        # requiring it here would turn guidance off for a caller who passes that output straight back in.
668	        has_neg_prompt = negative_prompt is not None or negative_prompt_embeds is not None
669	        do_true_cfg = true_cfg_scale > 1 and has_neg_prompt
670	        if true_cfg_scale > 1 and not has_neg_prompt:
671	            logger.warning(
672	                f"true_cfg_scale is passed as {true_cfg_scale}, but classifier-free guidance is not enabled since no "
673	                f"negative_prompt is provided."
674	            )
675	        elif true_cfg_scale <= 1 and has_neg_prompt:

677	                "negative_prompt is passed but classifier-free guidance is not enabled since true_cfg_scale <= 1"
678	            )
679	
680	        prompt_embeds, prompt_embeds_mask, image_pad_mask = self.encode_prompt(
681	            image=input_images,
682	            prompt=prompt,
683	            prompt_embeds=prompt_embeds,
684	            prompt_embeds_mask=prompt_embeds_mask,
685	            device=device,
686	            num_images_per_prompt=num_images_per_prompt,
687	        )
688	        if do_true_cfg:
689	            negative_prompt_embeds, negative_prompt_embeds_mask, negative_image_pad_mask = self.encode_prompt(
690	                image=input_images,
691	                prompt=negative_prompt,
692	                prompt_embeds=negative_prompt_embeds,
693	                prompt_embeds_mask=negative_prompt_embeds_mask,

699	        num_channels_latents = self.transformer.config.in_channels

701	            vae_images,

704	            height,

706	            prompt_embeds.dtype,
707	            device,
708	            generator,
709	            latents,
710	        )
711	
712	        img_shapes = [
713	            [
714	                *[
715	                    (1, vae_height // self.vae_scale_factor, vae_width // self.vae_scale_factor)
716	                    for vae_width, vae_height in input_image_sizes

718	                (1, height // self.vae_scale_factor, width // self.vae_scale_factor),
719	            ]
720	        ] * batch_size

722	        # 4. Prepare timesteps
723	        sigmas = np.linspace(1.0, 1 / num_inference_steps, num_inference_steps) if sigmas is None else sigmas
724	        mu = calculate_shift(
725	            latents.shape[1],
726	            self.scheduler.config.get("base_image_seq_len", 256),
727	            self.scheduler.config.get("max_image_seq_len", 4096),
728	            self.scheduler.config.get("base_shift", 0.5),
729	            self.scheduler.config.get("max_shift", 1.15),
730	        )
