13	// pushConstants mirrors the PC block in shaders/dit_common.glsl.
14	type pushConstants struct {
15		InOff, OutOff, WOff uint32
16		Tokens, Dim, Heads  uint32
17		HeadDim, Span       uint32
18		KOff, VOff, KStride uint32
19		Eps, Scale          uint32
20		Aux0, Aux1, Aux2    uint32
21		// The GEMM block, used only by dit_gemm.comp. Every pipeline in a graph
22		// shares one push-constant size (vk.DispatchMultiTimed records them into
23		// one command buffer), so these ride along on every dispatch whether or
24		// not it reads them.
25		BOff                uint32
26		GemmM, GemmN, GemmK uint32
27		LDA, LDB            uint32
28	}
29	
30	func (p pushConstants) bytes() []byte {
31		out := make([]byte, unsafe.Sizeof(p))
32		*(*pushConstants)(unsafe.Pointer(&out[0])) = p
33		return out
34	}
35	
36	// Kernel names one attention implementation. The scalar pair are kept
37	// alongside the matrix-core ladder on purpose: `KernelSimple` is small enough
38	// to read in one sitting, so it is the oracle the other two are checked
39	// against, and a disagreement between them is a bug in a kernel rather than a
40	// widening of everyone's tolerance.
41	type Kernel string
42	
43	const (
44		// KernelSimple is one query row per workgroup: shaders/dit_attention.comp.
45		KernelSimple Kernel = "simple"
46		// KernelFlash is the scalar tiled kernel with an online softmax:
47		// shaders/dit_attention_flash.comp.
48		KernelFlash Kernel = "flash"
49	)
50	
51	// wmmaVariant is one tile geometry of shaders/dit_attention_wmma.comp. The
52	// geometry is baked into the SPIR-V -- it sizes register and `shared` arrays --
53	// so as in bench/ops_gemm_wmma.go the Go side has to be told it rather than
54	// reading it back: qt gives the dispatch grid, and wave must match the -DWAVE
55	// the variant was built with or the workgroup stops being a single wave and
56	// two waves share the same LDS scratch.
57	type wmmaVariant struct {
58		name  Kernel
59		spirv []byte
60		qt    int    // query tiles per wave (16 rows each)
61		ktil  int    // key tiles per block
62		wave  uint32 // pinned subgroup size; 0 takes the driver's default (64 here)
63		// of16 is the same build with -DOUT_F16=1: the context written straight
64		// into the fp16 arena as the output projection's A operand instead of
65		// fp32 into the activation arena (stage 10). Nil on every variant that
66		// has no such build, and then GPUStack.FuseLayout keeps the narrowing
67		// pass. It is not a ladder rung -- same tiling, same speed on everything
68		// but the epilogue -- so it hangs off the variant rather than being one.
69		of16 []byte
70	}
71	
72	// rows is how many query rows one workgroup covers.
73	func (v wmmaVariant) rows() int { return v.qt * coopMatTile }
74	
75	// Intensity is the variant's arithmetic intensity in FLOP per byte of k and v
76	// read from global memory. Per key block a wave reads ktil*headDim/16
77	// fragments of each of k and v and issues 2*qt*ktil*headDim/16 multiplies, so
78	// ktil cancels and only qt moves the ratio -- which is why the ladder varies
79	// qt for intensity and ktil for register pressure, and why there is no third
80	// knob. The figure to beat is the ~28 FLOP/byte that saturates the MALL, and
81	// the scalar flash kernel's 2.67 (research/stage-3-dit-attention.md).
82	func (v wmmaVariant) Intensity() float64 { return float64(coopMatTile * v.qt) }
83	
84	// coopMatTile is the cooperative-matrix extent: 16x16x16 is the only shape
85	// this device reports, so it is a constant rather than a parameter, and
86	// NewGPUAttention checks that it is still true before building any variant.
87	const coopMatTile = 16
88	
89	// wmmaVariants is the stage-3c ladder, ordered so it reads off the results
90	// table: intensity 16 -> 32 -> 64 FLOP/byte at fixed ktil, then ktil varied at
91	// fixed intensity, then the wave32 arms (IDEAS §6.2). qt=4 was included
92	// expecting it to spill -- 32 accumulators plus 8 score tiles is past the
93	// wave64 register budget §2.7 ended on -- and it does, 361 VGPRs into scratch
94	// for 2.9x the time of qt=1. The measured table is in
95	// research/stage-3-dit-attention.md; the short version is that intensity does
96	// nothing here and the ladder is decided by spilling and by wave size.
97	var wmmaVariants = []wmmaVariant{
98		{name: "wmma_qt1_kt4", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT1KT4, qt: 1, ktil: 4},
99		{name: "wmma_qt2_kt4", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT2KT4, qt: 2, ktil: 4},
100		{name: "wmma_qt4_kt4", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT4KT4, qt: 4, ktil: 4},
101		{name: "wmma_qt2_kt2", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT2KT2, qt: 2, ktil: 2},
102		{name: "wmma_qt2_kt8", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT2KT8, qt: 2, ktil: 8},
103		{name: "wmma_qt1_kt8", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT1KT8, qt: 1, ktil: 8},
104		{name: "wmma_qt1_kt4_w32", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT1KT4W32, qt: 1, ktil: 4, wave: 32,
105			of16: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT1KT4W32OutF16},
106		{name: "wmma_qt2_kt4_w32", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT2KT4W32, qt: 2, ktil: 4, wave: 32},
107		{name: "wmma_qt1_kt2_w32", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT1KT2W32, qt: 1, ktil: 2, wave: 32},
108		{name: "wmma_qt1_kt8_w32", spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT1KT8W32, qt: 1, ktil: 8, wave: 32},
109	}
110	
111	// wmmaControl is the same kernel as wmma_qt2_kt4 with the tail mask compiled
112	// out (-DNO_TAIL_MASK). It is built and dispatchable but deliberately left out
113	// of wmmaVariants, so it never appears in Kernels() and no benchmark picks it
114	// up: its only caller is the negative control in gpu_test.go.
115	var wmmaControl = wmmaVariant{
116		name:  "wmma_qt2_kt4_nomask",
117		spirv: shaders.DiTAttentionWMMAQT2KT4NoMask,
118		qt:    2, ktil: 4,
119	}
120	
121	// controls are the other two deliberate breakages the negative control
122	// switches on. They live here rather than in the test because what they break
123	// is the dispatch -- which layout v is packed in, and whether q carries the
124	// log2(e) that makes the kernel's exp2 the right base -- and a test cannot
125	// reach either from outside Apply.
126	type controls struct {
127		// vNatural packs v in the same per-head layout as q and k instead of
128		// transposed, so p.v reduces over the wrong axis.
129		vNatural bool
130		// noLog2E drops log2(e) from q's scale, leaving the kernel computing
131		// 2^s where it should compute e^s.
132		noLog2E bool
133	}
134	
135	// DefaultKernel is the variant Apply uses unless told otherwise. It is the
136	// measured winner at 4096 tokens, which is the size that matters -- a 1024x1024
137	// latent is 4096 tokens and the caption stream's 320 is a rounding error beside
138	// it -- and it wins at 1024 and 2048 too: 6.64 ms against the runners-up's 9.1
139	// and the scalar flash kernel's 203.
140	//
141	// That the winner is the *lowest*-intensity geometry, at wave32, is the result
142	// of this stage. Arithmetic intensity was the whole story for the GEMM (§2.1)
143	// and it does nothing here: qt1, qt2 and qt4 span 16 to 64 FLOP/byte and land
144	// within 1.06x of each other at wave64. What moves the kernel is the register
145	// file -- qt4 spills and halves -- and the wave size, worth a clean 1.40x at
146	// the same tiling. K and V are read by every query block of the same head, so
147	// the caches supply the reuse that register blocking exists to provide, which
148	// is the same reason LDS staging lost in the GEMM.
149	const DefaultKernel Kernel = "wmma_qt1_kt4_w32"
150	
151	// GPUAttention runs the DiT's attention stack -- q/k RMS norms, rotary
152	// embedding and multi-head softmax attention -- on a Vulkan device.
153	//
154	// It takes q, k and v already projected. The projections are GEMMs, and
155	// wiring them to the register-blocked WMMA kernels is stage 4's job; keeping
156	// them out here means a failure in this code is a failure of the attention
157	// kernel and nothing else.
158	type GPUAttention struct {
159		dev  *vk.Device
160		wbuf *vk.Buffer
161		abuf *vk.Buffer
162		// hbuf is the fp16 arena the matrix-core kernels read: q and k packed
163		// per head, v packed per head and transposed. Nil when the device cannot
164		// run them, which is also what makes Kernels() shorter.
165		hbuf *vk.Buffer
166	
167		pipes map[string]*vk.ComputePipeline
168		mods  []*vk.ShaderModule
169		wmma  map[Kernel]wmmaVariant
170	
171		// Kernel selects the implementation. Defaults to DefaultKernel where the
172		// device can run it and KernelFlash where it cannot.
173		Kernel Kernel
174	
175		// ctl is empty in every real use; see controls.
176		ctl controls
177	
178		cfg     *Config
179		heads   int
180		headDim int
181		tokens  int
182		kStride int
183	
184		// Weight arena offsets.
185		normQOff, normKOff uint32
186		cosOff, sinOff     uint32
187	
188		// Activation arena offsets, all fixed for a given token count.
189		qOff, kOff, vOff, kTOff, outOff uint32
190		actElems                        int
191	
192		// fp16 arena: three planes of 16x16 fragment tiles, one per operand.
193		qhOff, khOff, vtOff uint32
194		tokPad              int
195		hElems              int
196	}
197	
198	// NewGPUAttention uploads the norm weights and the rotary table, and builds
199	// the pipelines for a fixed sequence length.
200	func NewGPUAttention(dev *vk.Device, attn *Attention, rope *RoPE, tokens int) (*GPUAttention, error) {
201		g := &GPUAttention{
202			dev:     dev,
203			pipes:   make(map[string]*vk.ComputePipeline),
204			wmma:    make(map[Kernel]wmmaVariant),
205			heads:   attn.Heads,
206			headDim: attn.HeadDim,
207			tokens:  tokens,
208		}
209		dim := attn.Heads * attn.HeadDim
210	
211		// Pad the transposed key stride off a multiple of the 4 KB channel
212		// rotation (IDEAS §5.1b). 64 floats is 256 B, which lands the gcd inside
213		// the [128, 256] window the rule wants.
214		g.kStride = tokens + 64
215	
216		var w []float32
217		put := func(v []float32) uint32 {
218			off := uint32(len(w))
219			w = append(w, v...)
220			return off
221		}
222		g.normQOff = put(attn.NormQ.Weight)
223		g.normKOff = put(attn.NormK.Weight)
224		g.cosOff = put(rope.Cos)
225		g.sinOff = put(rope.Sin)
226	
227		// Activation arena: q, k, v, the transposed keys, and the output.
228		alloc := func(n int) uint32 {
229			off := uint32(g.actElems)
230			g.actElems += (n + 63) &^ 63
231			return off
232		}
233		g.qOff = alloc(tokens * dim)
234		g.kOff = alloc(tokens * dim)
235		g.vOff = alloc(tokens * dim)
236		g.kTOff = alloc(attn.Heads * attn.HeadDim * g.kStride)
237		g.outOff = alloc(tokens * dim)
238	
239		var err error
240		if g.wbuf, err = dev.NewBuffer(len(w) * 4); err != nil {
241			g.Destroy()
242			return nil, fmt.Errorf("dit: weight buffer: %w", err)
243		}
244		g.wbuf.WriteFloat32(w)
245		if g.abuf, err = dev.NewBuffer(g.actElems * 4); err != nil {
246			g.Destroy()
247			return nil, fmt.Errorf("dit: activation buffer (%d MB): %w", (g.actElems*4)>>20, err)
248		}
249	
250		for name, spirv := range map[string][]byte{
251			"rmsnorm":            shaders.DiTRMSNorm,
252			"rope":               shaders.DiTRoPE,
253			"transpose":          shaders.DiTTransposeK,
254			string(KernelSimple): shaders.DiTAttention,
255			string(KernelFlash):  shaders.DiTAttentionFlash,
256		} {
257			if err := g.pipeline(name, spirv, vk.PipelineSpec{
258				Buffers:          []*vk.Buffer{g.wbuf, g.abuf},
259				PushConstantSize: uint32(unsafe.Sizeof(pushConstants{})),
260			}); err != nil {
261				g.Destroy()
262				return nil, err
263			}
264		}
265		g.Kernel = KernelFlash
266	
267		if err := g.buildWMMA(); err != nil {
268			g.Destroy()
269			return nil, err
270		}
271		return g, nil
272	}
273	
274	// pipeline compiles one shader module and its pipeline into g.
275	func (g *GPUAttention) pipeline(name string, spirv []byte, spec vk.PipelineSpec) error {
276		mod, err := g.dev.NewShaderModule(spirv)
277		if err != nil {
278			return fmt.Errorf("dit: shader %s: %w", name, err)
279		}
280		g.mods = append(g.mods, mod)
281		pipe, err := g.dev.NewPipeline(mod, spec)
282		if err != nil {
283			return fmt.Errorf("dit: pipeline %s: %w", name, err)
284		}
285		g.pipes[name] = pipe
286		return nil
287	}
288	
289	// canWMMA reports whether this device can run the matrix-core kernels at all:
290	// fp16 storage and arithmetic, cooperative matrices, and the 16x16x16
291	// fp16/fp32 shape every one of them has compiled in. A device reporting some
292	// other shape would run these shaders *wrong* rather than slowly, so the
293	// answer is "no" rather than "try it"; the scalar kernels still work, and the
294	// GEMM-bearing graph refuses to build instead.
295	func canWMMA(dev *vk.Device) (bool, error) {
296		feat := dev.Features()
297		if !feat.Float16 || !feat.CoopMatrix {
298			return false, nil
299		}
300		shapes, err := dev.Physical().CooperativeMatrixShapes()
301		if err != nil {
302			return false, fmt.Errorf("dit: cooperative-matrix shapes: %w", err)
303		}
304		for _, sh := range shapes {
305			if sh.Scope == vk.ScopeSubgroup && sh.M == coopMatTile && sh.N == coopMatTile && sh.K == coopMatTile &&
306				sh.AType == vk.ComponentFloat16 && sh.BType == vk.ComponentFloat16 &&
307				sh.CType == vk.ComponentFloat32 && sh.ResultType == vk.ComponentFloat32 {
308				return true, nil
309			}
310		}
311		return false, nil
312	}
313	
314	// buildWMMA allocates the fp16 arena and builds the matrix-core ladder, or
315	// does nothing at all if this device cannot run it. Not being able to is not
316	// an error: the scalar kernels still work, and a device that reports a
317	// cooperative-matrix shape other than 16x16x16 fp16/fp32 would run these
318	// shaders wrong rather than slowly, so it is skipped rather than trusted.
319	func (g *GPUAttention) buildWMMA() error {
320		ok, err := canWMMA(g.dev)
321		if err != nil {
322			return err
323		}
324		if !ok {
325			return nil
326		}
327		feat := g.dev.Features()
328		// HEAD_DIM is compiled into the shader, as the accumulator grid it sizes
329		// has to be known to the front end. Z-Image is 3840/30 = 128 everywhere.
330		if g.headDim != wmmaHeadDim {
331			return nil
332		}
333	
334		// fp16 arena. All three operands are stored as 16x16 fragment tiles --
335		// see shaders/dit_pack_f16.comp -- so the three planes are the same size
336		// and differ only in what one tile holds.
337		//
338		// tokPad rounds the sequence up so a workgroup's last query tile and a key
339		// block's tail read inside the arena rather than off the end; the padding
340		// is zeroed once here, so a pad key scores zero and the kernel's tail mask
341		// has something finite to work with.
342		g.tokPad = (g.tokens + wmmaTokenAlign - 1) &^ (wmmaTokenAlign - 1)
343	
344		plane := g.heads * g.tokPad * g.headDim
345		halloc := func(n int) uint32 {
346			off := uint32(g.hElems)
347			g.hElems += (n + 63) &^ 63
348			return off
349		}
350		g.qhOff = halloc(plane)
351		g.khOff = halloc(plane)
352		g.vtOff = halloc(plane)
353	
354		buf, err := g.dev.NewBuffer(g.hElems * 2)
355		if err != nil {
356			return fmt.Errorf("dit: fp16 arena (%d MB): %w", (g.hElems*2)>>20, err)
357		}
358		g.hbuf = buf
359		// Zero it once: the kernel reads the pad rows and columns, and fresh
360		// device memory is not specified to be zero.
361		g.hbuf.WriteFloat32(make([]float32, g.hElems/2))
362	
363		bufs := []*vk.Buffer{g.wbuf, g.abuf, g.hbuf}
364		pcSize := uint32(unsafe.Sizeof(pushConstants{}))
365		if err := g.pipeline("pack", shaders.DiTPackF16, vk.PipelineSpec{
366			Buffers: bufs, PushConstantSize: pcSize,
367		}); err != nil {
368			return err
369		}
370	
371		sgs, err := g.dev.Physical().SubgroupSizeControl()
372		if err != nil {
373			return fmt.Errorf("dit: subgroup size control: %w", err)
374		}
375		for _, v := range append(append([]wmmaVariant{}, wmmaVariants...), wmmaControl) {
376			// A wave32 variant is only correct if the size can actually be
377			// pinned: without it the driver would pack two waves into the
378			// 32-thread workgroup the SPIR-V declares.
379			if v.wave != 0 && (!feat.SubgroupSizeControl || !sgs.Supported ||
380				v.wave < sgs.MinSubgroupSize || v.wave > sgs.MaxSubgroupSize) {
381				continue
382			}
383			if err := g.pipeline(string(v.name), v.spirv, vk.PipelineSpec{
384				Buffers: bufs, PushConstantSize: pcSize, RequiredSubgroupSize: v.wave,
385			}); err != nil {
386				return err
387			}
388			g.wmma[v.name] = v
389		}
390		if _, ok := g.wmma[DefaultKernel]; ok {
391			g.Kernel = DefaultKernel
392		}
393		return nil
394	}
395	
396	// wmmaHeadDim is the head dimension compiled into
397	// shaders/dit_attention_wmma.comp (-DHEAD_DIM), and wmmaTokenAlign the
398	// sequence padding that covers every variant's query block and key block.
399	const (
400		wmmaHeadDim    = 128
401		wmmaTokenAlign = 128
402	)
403	
404	// Kernels lists the implementations this device can run, scalar first.
405	func (g *GPUAttention) Kernels() []Kernel {
406		out := []Kernel{KernelSimple, KernelFlash}
407		for _, v := range wmmaVariants {
408			if _, ok := g.wmma[v.name]; ok {
409				out = append(out, v.name)
410			}
411		}
412		return out
413	}
414	
415	// Destroy releases every Vulkan object.
416	func (g *GPUAttention) Destroy() {
417		for _, p := range g.pipes {
418			p.Destroy()
419		}
420		for _, m := range g.mods {
421			m.Destroy()
422		}
423		if g.hbuf != nil {
424			g.hbuf.Destroy()
425		}
426		if g.abuf != nil {
427			g.abuf.Destroy()
428		}
429		if g.wbuf != nil {
430			g.wbuf.Destroy()
431		}
432	}
433	
434	func groups(n, local int) uint32 { return uint32((n + local - 1) / local) }
435	
436	// flashQueryBlock must match QB in shaders/dit_attention_flash.comp.
437	const flashQueryBlock = 8
438	
439	// Apply runs the attention stack over already-projected q, k and v, each
440	// [tokens, heads*headDim]. normAndRope selects whether the q/k norms and the
441	// rotary embedding run, so the pieces can be checked separately.
442	func (g *GPUAttention) Apply(q, k, v *Mat, normAndRope bool) (*Mat, error) {
443		d, _, err := g.graph(q, k, v, normAndRope)
444		if err != nil {
445			return nil, err
446		}
447		// Batch the submits: a whole graph in one command buffer can exceed the
448		// driver's reset watchdog, which is how the VAE decoder first failed at
449		// 1024x1024 (PIPELINE.md).
450		const perSubmit = 8
451		for i := 0; i < len(d); i += perSubmit {
452			j := min(i+perSubmit, len(d))
453			if _, err := vk.DispatchMultiTimed(d[i:j], 1, 1, true); err != nil {
454				return nil, fmt.Errorf("dit: dispatch %d-%d: %w", i, j-1, err)
455			}
456		}
457		return g.result(), nil
458	}
459	
460	// Stage is one dispatch's identity and cost, as returned by Profile. Block is
461	// which block of a GPUStack it belongs to, and is zero for the attention
462	// stack's own profile, which has no blocks.
463	type Stage struct {
464		Index int
465		Block int
466		Kind  string
467		GPU   time.Duration
468	}
469	
470	// Profile runs the same graph Apply does, one dispatch at a time, and times
471	// each on the GPU. Wall-clock around Apply is not a measurement of the kernel:
472	// at 4096 tokens it also carries 189 MB of host writes for q, k and v and 63
473	// MB of read-back, which is how every tile geometry in the ladder came to look
474	// identical at 347 ms.
475	func (g *GPUAttention) Profile(q, k, v *Mat, normAndRope bool) ([]Stage, *Mat, error) {
476		d, kinds, err := g.graph(q, k, v, normAndRope)
477		if err != nil {
478			return nil, nil, err
479		}
480		stages := make([]Stage, 0, len(d))
481		for i := range d {
482			dur, err := vk.DispatchMultiTimed(d[i:i+1], 1, 1, true)
483			if err != nil {
484				return stages, nil, fmt.Errorf("dit: dispatch %d (%s): %w", i, kinds[i], err)
485			}
486			stages = append(stages, Stage{Index: i, Kind: kinds[i], GPU: dur})
487		}
488		return stages, g.result(), nil
489	}
490	
491	// result copies the output tensor out of the activation arena.
492	func (g *GPUAttention) result() *Mat {
493		dim := g.heads * g.headDim
494		out := NewMat(g.tokens, dim)
495		copy(out.Data, g.abuf.ReadFloat32At(int(g.outOff), g.tokens*dim))
496		return out
497	}
498	
499	// graph uploads q, k and v and builds the dispatch sequence for the selected
500	// kernel, with a label per dispatch. Apply and Profile share it so that what
501	// the profiler times is what Apply runs.
502	func (g *GPUAttention) graph(q, k, v *Mat, normAndRope bool) ([]vk.MultiDispatch, []string, error) {
503		dim := g.heads * g.headDim
504		if q.Rows != g.tokens || q.Cols != dim {
505			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("dit: q is %s, want [%d %d]", q, g.tokens, dim)
506		}
507		for name, m := range map[string]*Mat{"k": k, "v": v} {
508			if m.Rows != q.Rows || m.Cols != q.Cols {
509				return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("dit: %s is %s, want %s", name, m, q)
510			}
511		}
512		variant, isWMMA := g.wmma[g.Kernel]
513		if !isWMMA && g.Kernel != KernelSimple && g.Kernel != KernelFlash {
514			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("dit: no attention kernel %q (have %v)", g.Kernel, g.Kernels())
515		}
516	
517		g.abuf.WriteFloat32At(int(g.qOff), q.Data)
518		g.abuf.WriteFloat32At(int(g.kOff), k.Data)
519		g.abuf.WriteFloat32At(int(g.vOff), v.Data)
520	
521		base := pushConstants{
522			Tokens: uint32(g.tokens), Dim: uint32(dim),
523			Heads: uint32(g.heads), HeadDim: uint32(g.headDim),
524		}
525	
526		var d []vk.MultiDispatch
527		var kinds []string
528		add := func(pipe, kind string, gx, gy uint32, pc pushConstants) {
529			d = append(d, vk.MultiDispatch{Pipeline: g.pipes[pipe], GroupsX: gx, GroupsY: gy, PushConstants: pc.bytes()})
530			kinds = append(kinds, kind)
531		}
532	
533		if normAndRope {
534			// The q/k norms are per head, so the span is headDim and a row holds
535			// `heads` spans.
536			for i, s := range []struct {
537				off  uint32
538				wOff uint32
539			}{{g.qOff, g.normQOff}, {g.kOff, g.normKOff}} {
540				pc := base
541				pc.InOff, pc.OutOff, pc.WOff = s.off, s.off, s.wOff
542				pc.Span = uint32(g.headDim)
543				pc.Eps = math.Float32bits(float32(qkNormEps))
544				add("rmsnorm", []string{"rmsnorm q", "rmsnorm k"}[i], uint32(g.tokens*g.heads), 1, pc)
545			}
546			for i, off := range []uint32{g.qOff, g.kOff} {
547				pc := base
548				pc.InOff, pc.OutOff = off, off
549				pc.WOff, pc.Aux0 = g.cosOff, g.sinOff
550				add("rope", []string{"rope q", "rope k"}[i], groups(g.tokens*g.heads*g.headDim/2, 256), 1, pc)
551			}
552		}
553	
554		scale := float32(1 / math.Sqrt(float64(g.headDim)))
555		if isWMMA {
556			// Pack into the fp16 arena as fragment tiles. q carries the softmax
557			// scale and log2(e) with it, so the kernel's exponential is exp2 --
558			// one instruction on this ISA.
559			const log2e = 1.4426950408889634
560			for _, s := range []struct {
561				name     string
562				src, dst uint32
563				mode     uint32
564				scale    float32
565			}{
566				{"pack q", g.qOff, g.qhOff, 0, scale * log2e},
567				{"pack k", g.kOff, g.khOff, 0, 1},
568				{"pack v", g.vOff, g.vtOff, 1, 1},
569			} {
570				if s.dst == g.qhOff && g.ctl.noLog2E {
571					s.scale = scale
572				}
573				if s.dst == g.vtOff && g.ctl.vNatural {
574					s.mode = 0
575				}
576				pc := base
577				pc.InOff, pc.OutOff = s.src, s.dst
578				pc.Aux0, pc.Aux1 = s.mode, uint32(g.tokPad)
579				pc.Scale = math.Float32bits(s.scale)
580				// One workgroup per (token tile, head). The grid covers the
581				// padding as well as the sequence, so the pad tiles are rewritten
582				// as zeros rather than trusted to have stayed that way.
583				add("pack", s.name, groups(g.tokPad, coopMatTile), uint32(g.heads), pc)
584			}
585	
586			pc := base
587			pc.InOff, pc.OutOff = g.qhOff, g.outOff
588			pc.KOff, pc.VOff = g.khOff, g.vtOff
589			pc.Aux1 = uint32(g.tokPad)
590			add(string(variant.name), "attention", groups(g.tokens, variant.rows()), uint32(g.heads), pc)
591		} else {
592			// The scalar kernels read the keys transposed instead, in fp32.
593			pcT := base
594			pcT.InOff, pcT.OutOff = g.kOff, g.kTOff
595			pcT.KStride = uint32(g.kStride)
596			add("transpose", "transpose k", groups(g.tokens*dim, 256), 1, pcT)
597	
598			pc := base
599			pc.InOff, pc.OutOff = g.qOff, g.outOff
600			pc.KOff, pc.VOff, pc.KStride = g.kTOff, g.vOff, uint32(g.kStride)
601			pc.Scale = math.Float32bits(scale)
602			if g.Kernel == KernelFlash {
603				// One workgroup per QB query rows; QB is compiled into the shader.
604				add(string(KernelFlash), "attention", groups(g.tokens, flashQueryBlock), uint32(g.heads), pc)
605			} else {
606				add(string(KernelSimple), "attention", uint32(g.tokens), uint32(g.heads), pc)
607			}
608		}
609		return d, kinds, nil
610	}
611	
612	// Intensity is the named kernel's arithmetic intensity in FLOP per byte of k
613	// and v read from global memory, or 0 for the scalar kernels -- whose figure
614	// is a measurement rather than a property of the tiling, and lives in
615	// research/stage-3-dit-attention.md.
616	func (g *GPUAttention) Intensity(k Kernel) float64 {
617		if v, ok := g.wmma[k]; ok {
618			return v.Intensity()
619		}
620		return 0
621	}
622	
623	// ActivationBytes is the size of the activation arena.
624	func (g *GPUAttention) ActivationBytes() int { return g.abuf.Size() }
625

content.text:
**Q4 is done for t2i, and the vertical now has its headline number: a 1024²/40-step image's DiT runs in 90.7 seconds** — prefill 2.29 s, cached steps 2.27 s — against ~2.5 hours for our CPU oracle and ~35 minutes for torch's.

How it landed this cheaply (~750 lines + two small shaders, everything else reused from z-image's validated set):

- **`dit_final_norm.comp` turned out to be qi21's block pre-norm verbatim** — LayerNorm, non-affine, ×(1+scale), narrowed to the fp16 A operand — so every norm+modulate+narrow in the graph is one existing, negative-controlled shader.
- **The shared modulation never touches the GPU as compute**: ten host-computed vectors per step, with the t=0 row-selection expressed as two dispatch ranges over the same pipelines.
- **The SwiGLU fp16-range fix is exact**: scale by 1/16 into fp16, fold ×16 into the uploaded tanh(gate) vector — powers of two, no mantissa moved. (Z-image's norm-invariance trick was unavailable because 2.1's down-projection feeds a gated residual.)
- **New shaders, both small**: a scalar causal-attention fixup (the prefill runs the WMMA kernel bidirectionally over everything, then recomputes the ~20 text rows correctly — a fraction of a percent, once per image), and an offset copy for the KV cache (post-RoPE prefix k/v held as fp32 arena rows, restored under fresh target rows each step).

**Gates** — per the two-row-regime rule, both regimes measured against the oracle, and the 1024² run forced an honest distinction the first bound missed: *teacher-forced* error (the model, fed the oracle's own latents each step) is flat at 1.5e-3–8e-3 across all 40 steps; *free-running* error grows linearly at ~1.3e-3/step to 0.050 — trajectory divergence of a perturbed ODE, the same phenomenon diffusers documents for cache-on/off producing different-but-equally-valid samples. The test now bounds each separately. Correctness at 256² was right on the first run — the interface archaeology paid for itself.

**What stands between this and Q6 serving**: the VAE's GPU stage is now the critical path — the CPU decoder that took ~20 s at 256² extrapolates to minutes at 1024², which would dwarf the 91-second DiT. That, plus serving wiring, previews (Q7), and the deferred percents (tile re-screens at the big shapes, the full-seq re-pack, fusion ports) are what's left in the plan.

27	  — the **merged** diffusers implementation (PR

29	  copied verbatim 2026-09-20. This is the oracle every dump comes from.

43	
44	## The model, as the checkpoint describes it
45	
46	Three components, ~32.3 GB on disk (bf16), against Z-Image's ~20 GB resident:
47	
48	| | | |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| DiT | `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel` — **32 single-stream blocks**, dim 4096 (32 heads x 128), SwiGLU **12288** (mlp_ratio 3), **no biases anywhere**, per-head-dim q/k RMSNorm (eps 1e-6), 7.1 B params | 14 GB |
51	| Text encoder | **Qwen3-VL-8B** (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`): text model 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 q / 8 kv heads of 128, theta **5e6**, vocab 151936; plus a 27-layer vision tower (hidden 1152, patch 16, spatial-merge 2, deepstack taps at layers 8/16/24) | 17 GB |
52	| VAE | `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21` — Wan-lineage causal-3D residual conv AE, encoder base 96 / decoder base **144**, dim_mult [1,2,4,8,8], **z_dim 64, 16x spatial**, **4-channel RGBA in and out**, per-channel `latents_mean/std` (64 values each) | 1.3 GB |
53	
54	Geometry: **one latent token = one 16x16 pixel tile** (patch_size 1, VAE /16).
55	Pixel sides must be multiples of **32** (the VLM groups latent tokens 2x2).
56	1024² = 4096 image tokens — the same DiT sequence length as Z-Image at 1024².
57	2048² (the model's native size) = 16384. Defaults: **40 steps, no CFG**
58	(`true_cfg_scale=1.0`; true-CFG exists but is off by design), pipeline default
59	resolution **1024²** (the README's examples use 2048² explicitly).
60	
61	### The four mechanisms that make it different from Z-Image
62	
63	**1. One joint sequence, block-causal.** Text embeddings and image latents
64	share a single stream. The mask is `(q_idx >= kv_idx) OR same_image_block`:
65	the sequence is causal, text tokens strictly so, but every image block (each
66	condition image, and the target) is internally bidirectional. In diffusers the
67	non-flex processor decomposes this exactly into one attention call per prefix
68	segment (text segments get a causal triangle) plus one full-attention call for
69	the target — that decomposition, not a masked kernel, is the shape we port.
70	
71	**2. `causal_condition` + prefix KV cache.** Text and condition-image tokens
72	are modulated from **t = 0** (the modulation tensor carries batch+1 rows; the
73	target's tokens read their sample's row, everything else reads the t=0 row).
74	That makes the prefix's activations step-independent, so **step 0 runs the
75	full block-causal prefill and stores per-layer post-RoPE K/V for the prefix;
76	steps 1..N-1 recompute only the target's tokens**, attending over
77	[cached prefix K/V ++ fresh target K/V] with no mask at all (batch 1, no
78	padding). For t2i the prefix is just the prompt (tens of tokens — small win);
79	for edits it is thousands of tokens per reference image (large win). Caching
80	on/off changes rounding, not correctness — diffusers documents that the two
81	settings give *visibly different but equally valid* samples. **We ship
82	cache-on and validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`.**
83	
84	**3. Sequence assembly and RoPE.** The VLM sequence's `<|image_pad|>` slots
85	each stand for a **2x2 group of latent tokens**: the transformer expands those
86	positions four-fold and drops VAE latents into them; the target's slots are
87	appended after the text. Text embeddings pass through `txt_in` (zero-centered
88	RMSNorm → 4096→4096 → GELU-tanh → 4096→4096); latents through `img_in`
89	(64→4096, no bias). RoPE is 3-axis (frame/h/w, dims 16/56/56, theta 10000),
90	complex adjacent-pair rotation — **the same pairing as Z-Image's DiT**, not
91	the NeoX halves of the text encoder. Text advances all three axes together;
92	each image block freezes the frame axis and lays h/w out on a **zero-centered
93	grid with negative indices** (a flipped negative-frequency table serves
94	indices −1024..−1); after an image block the position cursor advances by
95	`max(h, w)`.
96	
97	**4. Shared modulation.** One `SiLU → Linear(4096→16384)` for the whole
98	model — blocks own no adaLN parameters. Each block chunks it into
99	(scale1, gate1, scale2, gate2); gates pass through **tanh**; norms are plain
100	non-affine LayerNorm. Final head: scale-only AdaLN + `proj_out` 4096→64.
101	Timestep embedding: sinusoidal 256 (cos first half — Z-Image convention
102	differs, check the dump), then a bias-free MLP to 4096.
103	
104	### Text encoding, exactly
105	
106	Raw template strings, **not** `apply_chat_template` (the two tokenize
107	differently and the checkpoint expects the raw form):
108	
109	```
110	t2i:  <|im_start|>system\nComprehend and analyze the provided prompt.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n{prompt}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n
111	edit: same, with "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" (then " <image2>…" etc.) prefixed to the user text
112	```
113	
114	- The embedding is the **last decoder layer's output *before* the final
115	  RMSNorm** (all 36 layers run — different from Z-Image's `hidden_states[-2]`
116	  where the last layer never ran). transformers 5.x silently normalizes
117	  `hidden_states[-1]`; diffusers neutralizes that with a forward hook on the
118	  final norm, and Q0 **verified the hook on transformers 5.17.0**: the hooked
119	  `hidden_states[-1]` equals the pipeline's output exactly (gap 0), so 5.17
120	  is the dump env — the model card requires >= 5.17 anyway.
121	- Drop the first `drop_idx` tokens, where drop_idx = length of the tokenized
122	  system message (computed, not hardcoded). Empty prompt becomes `" "`.
123	- For edits, condition images additionally go through the vision tower (RGBA
124	  flattened over white **for the vision copy only**); mrope with real 3D
125	  positions at image slots. Text-only prompts make mrope collapse to standard
126	  NeoX RoPE — **verified in Q0**: the model's own cos/sin tables for a text
127	  prompt match a plain theta-5e6 table to 0.0 (`mrope_gap` in the textenc
128	  manifest), so nothing mrope-shaped is needed before Q8.
129	- A fact Q8 rests on, confirmed while building the head dump: **the VLM's
130	  image-slot embedding rows are overwritten by the VAE latents** in the joint
131	  stream. Vision content reaches the DiT only through what the *text* tokens
132	  absorbed from the image inside the text encoder's own attention. The vision
133	  tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels.
134	
135	### Scheduler
136	
137	FlowMatchEulerDiscrete with **dynamic shifting**: sigmas `linspace(1, 1/N, N)`,
138	`mu` linear in the **target** token count between (256, 0.5) and (8192, 0.9)
139	— at 1024², mu = 0.6935, and **unclamped past 8192**: 2048² extrapolates to
140	mu = 1.3129 (measured, Q0) — `time_shift_type: exponential`,
141	`shift_terminal: 0.02`, `stochastic_sampling: false`. Port from diffusers'
142	scheduler, not from Z-Image's fixed shift 3.0. The scheduler steps **only the
143	target latents** (the model's output rows for the prefix are discarded).
144	VAE decode applies `z * std + mean` per channel; encode the inverse, and uses
145	the **posterior mode** (`argmax`), which keeps our seed-reproducibility rule
146	for free.
147	
148	---
149	
150	## What this changes about the vertical (semantics, not code)
151	
152	- **Edits stop being SDEdit.** Today an edit is a truncated generation
153	  (strength ⇒ steps skipped ⇒ cheaper). In 2.1 an edit is a *conditional
154	  generation*: reference latents + vision context as prefix, target from pure
155	  noise, all 40 steps. An edit becomes **slightly more expensive** than a
156	  generation (bigger prefix), the `strength` knob disappears, and up to **10
157	  reference images** arrive (OpenAI's `image[]` array already allows several).
158	  `/v1/images/edits` keeps its shape; its documentation changes meaning.
159	- **RGBA is native.** The VAE emits 4 channels always; transparency is asked
160	  for in the prompt (the model card's recommended phrasing). Map OpenAI's
161	  `background: "transparent"` to that prompt prefix + PNG-with-alpha out;
162	  opaque requests composite over white.
163	- **Masked / annotated local edits** (circles, painted regions, separate
164	  masks) are a *capability the model has* — the current 501 for masks may
165	  become closable. How a separate mask is fed (extra condition image?) is not
166	  in the diffusers PR; needs the examples repo before promising it (open
167	  question Q-o3).
168	- **The cost profile inverts.** Z-Image-Turbo was an 8-step distillation;
169	  2.1 wants 40 steps. Estimates (labeled, not measured): Z-Image's DiT step at
170	  1024²/4096 tokens is ~1.5 s on this machine; 2.1's blocks carry ~1.13x the
171	  parameters ⇒ ~1.7 s/step ⇒ **~70 s per 1024² image (vs 14.3 s today)**, and
172	  2048² (GEMMs x4, attention x16) lands around **5–6 min**. Text encode
173	  (~0.5–2 s) and VAE decode (~1–2 s at 1024²) are noise against that. The two
174	  levers, in order: **the step count** (sweep 40/24/16/12 for quality — knob
175	  already exists) and **a distilled/turbo release or LoRA** (the ecosystem
176	  around it — lightx2v etc. — is where Z-Image-Turbo itself came from; watch
177	  for it). This is the price of the capability jump and the user accepted the
178	  rework knowing the model; still, **Q6's first measurement decides the served
179	  defaults**, and 1024²/40 is the starting point, not a commitment.
180	
181	## The preview problem (taef1 has no successor here)
182	
183	`madebyollin/taehv`'s **taew2_1 does *not* fit this model**: it decodes the
184	Wan-2.1 16-channel/8x latent that the *original* Qwen-Image borrowed; 2.1's
185	VAE is a new 64-channel/16x RGBA design, and as of today taehv lists nothing
186	for it. So, in order:
187	
188	1. **Q7 ships a fitted linear preview**: a 64→3 (or →4) matrix, least-squares
189	   over dumped (latent, 1/16-scale image) pairs — the latent2rgb approach.
190	   One GEMV per pixel, effectively free per step; a 1024² generation previews
191	   at 64x64, upscaled client-side. Fitting data comes out of Q0's dumps.
192	2. **Watch taehv** for a 2.1 variant and port it like `zimage/vae/tiny.go`
193	   (at T=1 its temporal machinery degenerates; it would be a small 2D conv
194	   stack again). Do not build our own distilled decoder — that is a training
195	   project this repo does not want.
196	
197	## What survives, what is new, what dies
198	
199	| piece | verdict |
200	|---|---|
201	| `zimage/qwen` (Qwen3 text transformer, CPU + GPU) | **survives and grows** — it is shared infra (`embed`, `llm`, `parakeet` import it). Q1 adds: theta as config (5e6), 36-layer/pre-final-norm output mode beside the existing `EncoderLayers()` convention, and (Q8 only) mrope + deepstack + the vision tower. The Qwen3-Embedding caller must keep passing its tests untouched. |
202	| `zimage/tokenizer` | **survives** — same BPE family; new `added_tokens.json` (`<image1>`…, vision markers) and the raw template above. |
203	| shaders: `dit_gemm_*`, `dit_attention_*` (WMMA), gpu arenas | **survive** — new shapes 4096x4096 and 4096x12288 need a tile re-screen (`qwen.PlanFor` precedent; hypothesis 5 in `TODO.md` says wins don't transfer across M unmeasured). |
204	| `zimage/vae/gpu_conv*` | **survives as infrastructure** — the conv/groupnorm kernels feed the new VAE port. |
205	| `zimage/dit`, `zimage/vae` (model code), `zimage/pipeline` | **die** — replaced by a new `qimage/` tree (`qimage/dit`, `qimage/vae`, `qimage/pipeline`). New names because almost no line survives: different block, different mask, different VAE family. Delete z-image code as each Q-stage lands its replacement, not in one purge. |
206	| `cmd/zimage`, `cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/vaebench`, … | retargeted to `qimage` equivalents as their stage arrives. |
207	| `models/Z-Image-Turbo`, `models/taef1` (62 GB) | delete from disk once Q6 serves — not before, so A/B stays possible. |
208	| serving: `/v1/images/*`, streaming, geometry-under-a-ceiling | **survives in shape** — I1/I2's design carries over; the adapter re-wires to `qimage/pipeline`. |
209	
210	Two-machine deployment holds: image goes ~26 → **~36–40 GB resident**
211	(weights 32.3 GB fp16 + activations), sharing a 128 GB box with speech + TTS +
212	embeddings (~3 GB). Still no footprint quantisation.
213	
214	## The stages
215	
216	Same doctrine as every vertical: **CPU reference first, validated against a
217	dump, then the GPU port debugged against the CPU one.** One stage, one gate,
218	two-run numbers.
219	
220	- **Q0 — reference environment and dumps. Done 2026-09-20**, full-size
221	  oracle included: `out/qi21run1024` is the saved 1024²/40 fp32 CPU run
222	  (~52 s/step, ~35 min, ~68 GB — nothing else heavy may run beside it; a
223	  34 GB Go test alongside got both OOM-killed), and its PNG is a
224	  photorealistic render of the prompt. The env: the shared `.venv` with torch
225	  2.14.0+cpu, transformers 5.17.0, torchvision 0.29.0+cpu, accelerate, and
226	  **diffusers 0.41.0.dev0 pinned to git commit `80c7ed26`** (stable 0.40.0
227	  predates the merge); `reference/qwenimage21/` is byte-identical to the
228	  installed package. Five scripts, all fp32 CPU, all in `reference/`:
229	  - `dump_qi21_sched.py` → `out/qi21sched` — sigma/timestep tables for five
230	    size/step cases plus one Euler step over deterministic vectors.
231	  - `dump_qi21_dit.py` → `out/qi21dit` — everything around the blocks
232	    (num_layers=0, 9 tensors): txt_in/img_in, joint assembly, RoPE tables,
233	    image_ids/target mask, the t=0 modulation row, prefill and cached
234	    forwards, for a t2i case and a synthetic edit case. The
235	    prefill-vs-cached identity at 0 blocks measured exactly 0.
236	  - `dump_qi21_dit_block.py` → `out/qi21block` — block 0 with real weights
237	    in prefill/extract/cached modes, cache K/V contents included; the fp32
238	    cached-vs-prefill gap on target rows measured **≤ 3.8e-6** (t2i), 0
239	    (edit) — Q4's numeric bound.
240	  - `dump_qi21_vae.py` → `out/qi21vae` — decode from seeded noise and encode
241	    of a deterministic RGBA test card (posterior **mode**), per-child and
242	    per-up/down-block intermediates hooked, 256² and 192x320. Decode clamps
243	    to [-1,1]; encoder conv_out is 128 = 64 mean + 64 logvar.
244	  - `dump_qi21_run.py` → `out/qi21run` + `out/qi21run2` — the end-to-end
245	    oracle: 256²/4 steps, seed 42, kv-cache on, noise passed in packed (the
246	    Go side gets it as data, not torch RNG), per-step latents, final RGBA
247	    image + PNG. **Two runs byte-identical**, and the PNG is recognizably
248	    the prompt. `--size 1024 --steps 40 --out out/qi21run1024` is the saved
249	    full-size run.
250	  - `dump_qi21_textenc.py` → `out/qi21textenc` — runs the pipeline's own
251	    `_get_qwen_prompt_embeds` (en / cjk / empty prompts), plus a layer walk
252	    (embed, layers 0-1, last-prenorm) and the rope cos/sin capture that
253	    settled Q-o5. drop_idx = 14 for the shipped system prompt.
254	- **Q1 — text encoding in Go. Done 2026-09-20.** `zimage/qwen` needed **no
255	  change at all** — `qimage/textenc` (the tree's first package) supplies the
256	  nested-`text_config` adapter (Prefix `model.language_model.`), the raw t2i
257	  template, the tokenized-system-message drop, and `Drop`; `Load(dir,
258	  cfg.NumLayers)` already expresses "all 36 layers, no final norm". Gates:
259	  tokenizer exact on en/cjk/empty; layer walk ≤ 2e-5; **CPU encoder en
260	  1.6e-4 / cjk 8.6e-5 / empty 7.1e-4 against a `deepTol` of 1e-3** — measured,
261	  not chosen: the reference disagrees with *itself* by 3.2e-4 on the empty
262	  prompt when only the attention kernel changes (eager vs sdpa), so
263	  z-image's 2e-4 sits below this model's own fp32 noise floor at depth 36.
264	  **GPU encoder (fp16, unchanged kernels) en/cjk 0.024-0.027, empty 0.21**,
265	  and that number has a mechanism (`TestGPULadder`, kept as the permanent
266	  instrument): the residual stream grows a ~13k massive-activation channel
267	  at layer 6, carries it flat, and **cancels it in layers 34-35 — the two
268	  layers Z-Image never ran** — so the fp16 bulk-rounding variance the
269	  channel accumulated surfaces at the end (protecting just the spike
270	  elements measurably does not help). Priced against deployment: the
271	  **official bf16 pipeline deviates from fp32 by rel 2.0 (abs 204)** through
272	  the same mechanism — our fp16 path is 10-85x closer to fp32 than what the
273	  ecosystem ships. Not taken (priced): an fp32-activation GEMM arm for the
274	  encoder — at prompt-sized M (~40 rows) the encoder is weight-bandwidth-
275	  bound so it would be cheap; build it only if Q3/Q6 show prompt adherence
276	  suffering.
277	- **Q2 — one DiT block on CPU. Done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/dit`): layout
278	  (image ids/target mask/segments) **exact** vs the dump, RoPE tables at
279	  ~5e-7 (negative-index grids included), head pieces at ~1e-5, the no-block
280	  prefill/cached forwards at ~4e-6, and the block gate — out_prefill,
281	  cache K/V contents, out_cached, both cases — at **≤ 4e-5** against
282	  `out/qi21block`. The negative control (NeoX-halves rotary pairing) is
283	  caught at 1e5x the bound. `Load(dir, blocks)` takes 0/1/32 blocks, so Q3's
284	  stack is a loop away. One porting trap found and worth remembering:
285	  `chunk(2, -1)` splits *rows* — rewrapping the modulation's backing array
286	  at half width hands row 1 the second half of row 0, and every downstream
287	  tensor fails at rel ~10 while every shape checks out.
288	- **Q3 — the stack + scheduler + t2i sampler on CPU. Done 2026-09-20 at the
289	  latent gate** (`qimage/pipeline`): the dynamic-shift scheduler matches
290	  diffusers at ~1e-6 across all five dumped size/step cases (mu exact, the
291	  exponential shift, the terminal stretch, the Euler step), and
292	  `Denoise` — 32 blocks, ModeExtract at step 0 then cached decodes, exactly
293	  as served — reproduces the 256²/4-step oracle's **per-step latents at
294	  rel 2.1e-5 → 2.5e-4** (bound 1e-3, 4x measured; 2.3 min a sample on CPU).
295	  **Still owed to Q5**: the *image* gate — prompt → PNG with our own text
296	  encoder and VAE decode against the oracle's `image` tensor (Z-Image's
297	  2.2e-2 precedent). The three green gates (textenc, denoise, decoder) do
298	  not compose into that claim; it gets measured, once the decoder exists.
299	- **Q4 — DiT on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20 for t2i** (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`,
300	  ~750 lines on z-image's shader set): **1024²/40 steps in 90.7 s — prefill
301	  2.29 s, cached steps 2.27 s** — against CPU Go's ~2.5 h and torch fp32's
302	  ~35 min. The mapping that made it small: the block's LayerNorm+modulate+
303	  narrow is `dit_final_norm.comp` verbatim; the shared modulation is host
304	  arithmetic (ten uploaded vectors) with the t=0 row-select expressed as two
305	  dispatch ranges; SwiGLU's fp16 range problem is solved *exactly* by
306	  scaling 1/16 into fp16 and folding 16 into the uploaded tanh(gate) vector
307	  (2.1's down-proj feeds a gated residual, so z-image's norm-invariance
308	  trick was unavailable). Two new shaders: `dit_attn_causal.comp` (the
309	  prefill runs the WMMA kernel bidirectionally over the whole sequence and
310	  this recomputes the text rows' context causally — tens of rows, once per
311	  image) and `dit_copy.comp` (offset copies for the KV cache). The cache is
312	  each block's post-RoPE prefix k/v as fp32 arena rows, restored under the
313	  fresh target rows each step before a full re-pack (fine at t2i's tiny
314	  prefix; Q8's reference images want it fp16 + tile-masked, and the
315	  full-seq re-pack is a Q9 percent). **Gates, per
316	  `two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate`, both regimes against the oracle**:
317	  teacher-forced (each step fed the oracle's own latents — bounds the
318	  model) flat at 1.5e-3–8e-3 over all 40 steps at 1024², bound 2e-2;
319	  free-running drifts linearly at ~1.3e-3/step to 0.050 at 40 steps — a
320	  perturbed ODE diverging, the phenomenon diffusers documents for
321	  cache-on/off — bounded at 0.12 with the image judgment deferred to Q6's
322	  eyeball. Not done: tile re-screen at M=16384/K=12288 (running on
323	  z-image's measured winners uncontested — a Q9 percent), the VAE's GPU
324	  stage (with Q5's fp16-range constraint), and the negative-control
325	  breakages the z-image graph carries.
326	- **Q5 — the VAE in Go. CPU done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/vae`, on
327	  `zimage/vae`'s Tensor/Conv2D — whose Pad/PadEnd/Stride already carried the
328	  identical downsampler shape): decoder and encoder, stagewise against
329	  `out/qi21vae`, RGBA round trip included. The T=1 semantics are explicit in
330	  the package doc: causal 3D convs fold to 2D, time_convs never run,
331	  AvgDown3D *means in a zero frame* on temporal blocks, DupUp3D keeps only
332	  the last temporal copy. Two measured bounds: conv stages at 2e-4 (they run
333	  at ≤5e-5), and `normTol` 8e-3 for the stages where the model amplifies
334	  fp32 noise — the decoder past its per-pixel L2 tail norm (the dumped fp32
335	  reference is itself rel 1.3e-3 from a float64 decode there; our decoded
336	  image sits max abs 8.7e-4 from the dump, under a quarter of one 8-bit
337	  step) and the encoder's deep middle (the reference's own thread-order
338	  noise jumps 47x at down_blocks.3; we track ~5x that and land at 4.7e-5 on
339	  the posterior mode).
340	  **The end-to-end image gate Q3 owed is closed**: `TestEndToEndImage` runs
341	  prompt → image through our tokenizer, text encoder, DiT, scheduler and
342	  decoder — only the noise is the oracle's — and matches the 256²/4-step
343	  reference image at **max abs 9.1e-4, mean 6e-6** in [0, 1] space, 24x
344	  inside the 2.2e-2 precedent. (~65 GB fp32 passes through, sequenced to a
345	  ~34 GB peak; it must run alone.)
346	  **Still open in Q5: the GPU port**, which folds into Q4's GPU stage — and
347	  the fp16 constraint from Q0 stands: decoder intermediates reach absmax
348	  ~1e5–3e5 against fp16's 65504, so those stages need fp32 storage or a
349	  rescale, unlike z-image's decoder.
350	- **Q6 — serve t2i.** `-image` loads qimage; `/v1/images/generations` with
351	  geometry under a ceiling (multiples of 32 now, not 16), `background:
352	  "transparent"`, steps default 40. **First honest wall clock** (two runs) at
353	  1024² and 2048², and the **step-count sweep** (40/24/16/12, same seed,
354	  eyeball + a fixed prompt set) that decides the served default. Delete
355	  Z-Image weights and dead code after this lands.
356	- **Q7 — previews.** Fit the linear 64→RGB matrix from Q0's pairs, wire
357	  `stream: true`/`partial_images` back up.
358	- **Q8 — edits.** The big one, in three parts: (a) VAE encoder serving
359	  reference latents (Q5 built it), (b) **the vision tower** — 27-layer ViT,
360	  2x2 spatial merge, interpolated position grid, deepstack feature injection
361	  into the text model's first layers, mrope with real 3D positions — the
362	  largest genuinely new port in this migration, (c) multi-image template +
363	  per-ref RoPE blocks + prefix cache across refs. `/v1/images/edits` drops
364	  `strength`, gains multi-ref. Gate: edit dump match + an end-to-end edit vs
365	  the oracle.
366	- **Q9 — percents.** Only after capabilities: the I3/I5/I8/I9 fusion lesson
367	  (elementwise passes absorbed into consumers) transfers to a new but
368	  same-shaped budget; attribute before optimising, same-hour controls, plans
369	  measured never composed.
370	
371	## Decisions taken now (so future sessions don't relitigate)
372	
373	1. **New `qimage/` tree; `zimage/qwen` and `zimage/tokenizer` stay put** until
374	   z-image is fully gone, then a mechanical rename can hoist them.
375	2. **KV cache always on** — validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`;
376	   cache-off exists only as a debug path if Q4 needs it.
377	3. **Posterior mode (argmax) for every VAE encode** — matches the reference
378	   and our reproducibility rule.
379	4. **1024² default, 2048² behind the ceiling flag**, pending Q6's numbers.
380	5. **No self-trained tiny decoder**; linear preview + watch taehv.
381	6. **No CFG path in the Go port** (true_cfg_scale stays a refusal if asked
382	   for over HTTP) until something demands it — it would double every step.
383	
384	## Open questions
385	
386	- **Q-o1**: how far below 40 steps does quality hold? (Q6 sweep; also decides
387	  whether the vertical's headline is ~30 s or ~70 s.)
388	- **Q-o2**: does a turbo/distilled 2.1 checkpoint or step-distillation LoRA
389	  appear? (Watch the examples repo and lightx2v.)
390	- **Q-o3**: how are separate masks / painted annotations fed for local edits?
391	  (Examples repo, before `/v1/images/edits` promises masks.)
392	- **Q-o4**: does taehv grow a 2.1 variant? (Q7 fallback becomes an upgrade.)
393	- ~~**Q-o5**: text-only mrope — confirmed equivalent to plain RoPE by dump?~~
394	  **Settled 2026-09-20 (Q0)**: gap 0.0 against a plain theta-5e6 NeoX table;
395	  `zimage/qwen` needs nothing mrope-shaped before Q8.

# IMAGE — the Qwen-Image-2.1 vertical

> **Written 2026-09-20, plan only — nothing is built.** This file is live
> again: the old root `IMAGE.md` was frozen into
> [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md) at the 2026-09-20
> consolidation, and this new one plans the **replacement of Z-Image-Turbo by
> `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`** for both generation and edits. Same rules as every
> vertical file: rewritten each session, not appended to; closed stages go to
> `research/`. Stage letters here are **Q0, Q1, …** (I-stages stay z-image's,
> in the archive).
>
> Breaking the current vertical while we do this is accepted up front
> (2026-09-20 session). Z-Image code gets deleted, not kept in parallel —
> except `zimage/qwen`, which `embed`, `llm` and `parakeet` also import
> (see "what survives").

**Target**: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` — prompt → PNG (optionally RGBA) at up to
2048x2048, and native reference-image editing (up to 10 refs), end to end in
Go on Vulkan, served at `POST /v1/images/generations` and

## The model, as the checkpoint describes it

Three components, ~32.3 GB on disk (bf16), against Z-Image's ~20 GB resident:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| DiT | `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel` — **32 single-stream blocks**, dim 4096 (32 heads x 128), SwiGLU **12288** (mlp_ratio 3), **no biases anywhere**, per-head-dim q/k RMSNorm (eps 1e-6), 7.1 B params | 14 GB |
| Text encoder | **Qwen3-VL-8B** (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`): text model 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 q / 8 kv heads of 128, theta **5e6**, vocab 151936; plus a 27-layer vision tower (hidden 1152, patch 16, spatial-merge 2, deepstack taps at layers 8/16/24) | 17 GB |
| VAE | `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21` — Wan-lineage causal-3D residual conv AE, encoder base 96 / decoder base **144**, dim_mult [1,2,4,8,8], **z_dim 64, 16x spatial**, **4-channel RGBA in and out**, per-channel `latents_mean/std` (64 values each) | 1.3 GB |

Geometry: **one latent token = one 16x16 pixel tile** (patch_size 1, VAE /16).
Pixel sides must be multiples of **32** (the VLM groups latent tokens 2x2).
1024² = 4096 image tokens — the same DiT sequence length as Z-Image at 1024².
2048² (the model's native size) = 16384. Defaults: **40 steps, no CFG**
(`true_cfg_scale=1.0`; true-CFG exists but is off by design), pipeline default
resolution **1024²** (the README's examples use 2048² explicitly).

### The four mechanisms that make it different from Z-Image

**1. One joint sequence, block-causal.** Text embeddings and image latents
share a single stream. The mask is `(q_idx >= kv_idx) OR same_image_block`:
the sequence is causal, text tokens strictly so, but every image block (each
condition image, and the target) is internally bidirectional. In diffusers the
non-flex processor decomposes this exactly into one attention call per prefix
segment (text segments get a causal triangle) plus one full-attention call for
the target — that decomposition, not a masked kernel, is the shape we port.

**2. `causal_condition` + prefix KV cache.** Text and condition-image tokens
are modulated from **t = 0** (the modulation tensor carries batch+1 rows; the
target's tokens read their sample's row, everything else reads the t=0 row).
That makes the prefix's activations step-independent, so **step 0 runs the
full block-causal prefill and stores per-layer post-RoPE K/V for the prefix;
steps 1..N-1 recompute only the target's tokens**, attending over
[cached prefix K/V ++ fresh target K/V] with no mask at all (batch 1, no
padding). For t2i the prefix is just the prompt (tens of tokens — small win);
for edits it is thousands of tokens per reference image (large win). Caching
on/off changes rounding, not correctness — diffusers documents that the two
settings give *visibly different but equally valid* samples. **We ship
cache-on and validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`.**

**3. Sequence assembly and RoPE.** The VLM sequence's `<|image_pad|>` slots
each stand for a **2x2 group of latent tokens**: the transformer expands those
positions four-fold and drops VAE latents into them; the target's slots are
appended after the text. Text embeddings pass through `txt_in` (zero-centered
RMSNorm → 4096→4096 → GELU-tanh → 4096→4096); latents through `img_in`
(64→4096, no bias). RoPE is 3-axis (frame/h/w, dims 16/56/56, theta 10000),
complex adjacent-pair rotation — **the same pairing as Z-Image's DiT**, not
the NeoX halves of the text encoder. Text advances all three axes together;
each image block freezes the frame axis and lays h/w out on a **zero-centered
grid with negative indices** (a flipped negative-frequency table serves
indices −1024..−1); after an image block the position cursor advances by
`max(h, w)`.

**4. Shared modulation.** One `SiLU → Linear(4096→16384)` for the whole
model — blocks own no adaLN parameters. Each block chunks it into
(scale1, gate1, scale2, gate2); gates pass through **tanh**; norms are plain
non-affine LayerNorm. Final head: scale-only AdaLN + `proj_out` 4096→64.
Timestep embedding: sinusoidal 256 (cos first half — Z-Image convention
differs, check the dump), then a bias-free MLP to 4096.

### Text encoding, exactly

Raw template strings, **not** `apply_chat_template` (the two tokenize
differently and the checkpoint expects the raw form):

```
t2i:  <|im_start|>system\nComprehend and analyze the provided prompt.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n{prompt}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n
edit: same, with "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" (then " <image2>…" etc.) prefixed to the user text
```

- The embedding is the **last decoder layer's output *before* the final
  RMSNorm** (all 36 layers run — different from Z-Image's `hidden_states[-2]`
  where the last layer never ran). transformers 5.x silently normalizes
  `hidden_states[-1]`; diffusers neutralizes that with a forward hook on the
  final norm, and Q0 **verified the hook on transformers 5.17.0**: the hooked
  `hidden_states[-1]` equals the pipeline's output exactly (gap 0), so 5.17
  is the dump env — the model card requires >= 5.17 anyway.
- Drop the first `drop_idx` tokens, where drop_idx = length of the tokenized
  system message (computed, not hardcoded). Empty prompt becomes `" "`.
- For edits, condition images additionally go through the vision tower (RGBA
  flattened over white **for the vision copy only**); mrope with real 3D
  positions at image slots. Text-only prompts make mrope collapse to standard
  NeoX RoPE — **verified in Q0**: the model's own cos/sin tables for a text
  prompt match a plain theta-5e6 table to 0.0 (`mrope_gap` in the textenc
  manifest), so nothing mrope-shaped is needed before Q8.
- A fact Q8 rests on, confirmed while building the head dump: **the VLM's
  image-slot embedding rows are overwritten by the VAE latents** in the joint
  stream. Vision content reaches the DiT only through what the *text* tokens
  absorbed from the image inside the text encoder's own attention. The vision
  tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels.

### Scheduler

FlowMatchEulerDiscrete with **dynamic shifting**: sigmas `linspace(1, 1/N, N)`,
`mu` linear in the **target** token count between (256, 0.5) and (8192, 0.9)
— at 1024², mu = 0.6935, and **unclamped past 8192**: 2048² extrapolates to
mu = 1.3129 (measured, Q0) — `time_shift_type: exponential`,
`shift_terminal: 0.02`, `stochastic_sampling: false`. Port from diffusers'
scheduler, not from Z-Image's fixed shift 3.0. The scheduler steps **only the
target latents** (the model's output rows for the prefix are discarded).
VAE decode applies `z * std + mean` per channel; encode the inverse, and uses
the **posterior mode** (`argmax`), which keeps our seed-reproducibility rule
for free.

---

## What this changes about the vertical (semantics, not code)

- **Edits stop being SDEdit.** Today an edit is a truncated generation
  (strength ⇒ steps skipped ⇒ cheaper). In 2.1 an edit is a *conditional
  generation*: reference latents + vision context as prefix, target from pure
  noise, all 40 steps. An edit becomes **slightly more expensive** than a
  generation (bigger prefix), the `strength` knob disappears, and up to **10
  reference images** arrive (OpenAI's `image[]` array already allows several).
  `/v1/images/edits` keeps its shape; its documentation changes meaning.
- **RGBA is native.** The VAE emits 4 channels always; transparency is asked
  for in the prompt (the model card's recommended phrasing). Map OpenAI's
  `background: "transparent"` to that prompt prefix + PNG-with-alpha out;
  opaque requests composite over white.
- **Masked / annotated local edits** (circles, painted regions, separate
  masks) are a *capability the model has* — the current 501 for masks may
  become closable. How a separate mask is fed (extra condition image?) is not
  in the diffusers PR; needs the examples repo before promising it (open
  question Q-o3).
- **The cost profile inverts.** Z-Image-Turbo was an 8-step distillation;
  2.1 wants 40 steps. Estimates (labeled, not measured): Z-Image's DiT step at
  1024²/4096 tokens is ~1.5 s on this machine; 2.1's blocks carry ~1.13x the
  parameters ⇒ ~1.7 s/step ⇒ **~70 s per 1024² image (vs 14.3 s today)**, and
  2048² (GEMMs x4, attention x16) lands around **5–6 min**. Text encode
  (~0.5–2 s) and VAE decode (~1–2 s at 1024²) are noise against that. The two
  levers, in order: **the step count** (sweep 40/24/16/12 for quality — knob
  already exists) and **a distilled/turbo release or LoRA** (the ecosystem
  around it — lightx2v etc. — is where Z-Image-Turbo itself came from; watch
  for it). This is the price of the capability jump and the user accepted the
  rework knowing the model; still, **Q6's first measurement decides the served
  defaults**, and 1024²/40 is the starting point, not a commitment.

## The preview problem (taef1 has no successor here)

`madebyollin/taehv`'s **taew2_1 does *not* fit this model**: it decodes the
Wan-2.1 16-channel/8x latent that the *original* Qwen-Image borrowed; 2.1's
VAE is a new 64-channel/16x RGBA design, and as of today taehv lists nothing
for it. So, in order:

1. **Q7 ships a fitted linear preview**: a 64→3 (or →4) matrix, least-squares
   over dumped (latent, 1/16-scale image) pairs — the latent2rgb approach.
   One GEMV per pixel, effectively free per step; a 1024² generation previews
   at 64x64, upscaled client-side. Fitting data comes out of Q0's dumps.
2. **Watch taehv** for a 2.1 variant and port it like `zimage/vae/tiny.go`
   (at T=1 its temporal machinery degenerates; it would be a small 2D conv
   stack again). Do not build our own distilled decoder — that is a training
   project this repo does not want.

| piece | verdict |
|---|---|
| `zimage/qwen` (Qwen3 text transformer, CPU + GPU) | **survives and grows** — it is shared infra (`embed`, `llm`, `parakeet` import it). Q1 adds: theta as config (5e6), 36-layer/pre-final-norm output mode beside the existing `EncoderLayers()` convention, and (Q8 only) mrope + deepstack + the vision tower. The Qwen3-Embedding caller must keep passing its tests untouched. |
| `zimage/tokenizer` | **survives** — same BPE family; new `added_tokens.json` (`<image1>`…, vision markers) and the raw template above. |
| shaders: `dit_gemm_*`, `dit_attention_*` (WMMA), gpu arenas | **survive** — new shapes 4096x4096 and 4096x12288 need a tile re-screen (`qwen.PlanFor` precedent; hypothesis 5 in `TODO.md` says wins don't transfer across M unmeasured). |
| `zimage/vae/gpu_conv*` | **survives as infrastructure** — the conv/groupnorm kernels feed the new VAE port. |
| `zimage/dit`, `zimage/vae` (model code), `zimage/pipeline` | **die** — replaced by a new `qimage/` tree (`qimage/dit`, `qimage/vae`, `qimage/pipeline`). New names because almost no line survives: different block, different mask, different VAE family. Delete z-image code as each Q-stage lands its replacement, not in one purge. |

Two-machine deployment holds: image goes ~26 → **~36–40 GB resident**
(weights 32.3 GB fp16 + activations), sharing a 128 GB box with speech + TTS +

## The stages

Same doctrine as every vertical: **CPU reference first, validated against a
dump, then the GPU port debugged against the CPU one.** One stage, one gate,
two-run numbers.

- **Q0 — reference environment and dumps. Done 2026-09-20**, full-size
  oracle included: `out/qi21run1024` is the saved 1024²/40 fp32 CPU run
  (~52 s/step, ~35 min, ~68 GB — nothing else heavy may run beside it; a
  34 GB Go test alongside got both OOM-killed), and its PNG is a
  photorealistic render of the prompt. The env: the shared `.venv` with torch
  2.14.0+cpu, transformers 5.17.0, torchvision 0.29.0+cpu, accelerate, and
  **diffusers 0.41.0.dev0 pinned to git commit `80c7ed26`** (stable 0.40.0
  predates the merge); `reference/qwenimage21/` is byte-identical to the
  installed package. Five scripts, all fp32 CPU, all in `reference/`:
  - `dump_qi21_sched.py` → `out/qi21sched` — sigma/timestep tables for five
    size/step cases plus one Euler step over deterministic vectors.
  - `dump_qi21_dit.py` → `out/qi21dit` — everything around the blocks
    (num_layers=0, 9 tensors): txt_in/img_in, joint assembly, RoPE tables,
    image_ids/target mask, the t=0 modulation row, prefill and cached
    forwards, for a t2i case and a synthetic edit case. The
    prefill-vs-cached identity at 0 blocks measured exactly 0.
  - `dump_qi21_dit_block.py` → `out/qi21block` — block 0 with real weights
    in prefill/extract/cached modes, cache K/V contents included; the fp32
    cached-vs-prefill gap on target rows measured **≤ 3.8e-6** (t2i), 0
    (edit) — Q4's numeric bound.
  - `dump_qi21_vae.py` → `out/qi21vae` — decode from seeded noise and encode
    of a deterministic RGBA test card (posterior **mode**), per-child and
    per-up/down-block intermediates hooked, 256² and 192x320. Decode clamps
    to [-1,1]; encoder conv_out is 128 = 64 mean + 64 logvar.
  - `dump_qi21_run.py` → `out/qi21run` + `out/qi21run2` — the end-to-end
    oracle: 256²/4 steps, seed 42, kv-cache on, noise passed in packed (the
    Go side gets it as data, not torch RNG), per-step latents, final RGBA
    image + PNG. **Two runs byte-identical**, and the PNG is recognizably
    the prompt. `--size 1024 --steps 40 --out out/qi21run1024` is the saved
    full-size run.
  - `dump_qi21_textenc.py` → `out/qi21textenc` — runs the pipeline's own
    `_get_qwen_prompt_embeds` (en / cjk / empty prompts), plus a layer walk
    (embed, layers 0-1, last-prenorm) and the rope cos/sin capture that
    settled Q-o5. drop_idx = 14 for the shipped system prompt.
- **Q1 — text encoding in Go. Done 2026-09-20.** `zimage/qwen` needed **no
  change at all** — `qimage/textenc` (the tree's first package) supplies the
  nested-`text_config` adapter (Prefix `model.language_model.`), the raw t2i
  template, the tokenized-system-message drop, and `Drop`; `Load(dir,
  cfg.NumLayers)` already expresses "all 36 layers, no final norm". Gates:
  tokenizer exact on en/cjk/empty; layer walk ≤ 2e-5; **CPU encoder en
  1.6e-4 / cjk 8.6e-5 / empty 7.1e-4 against a `deepTol` of 1e-3** — measured,
  not chosen: the reference disagrees with *itself* by 3.2e-4 on the empty
  prompt when only the attention kernel changes (eager vs sdpa), so
  z-image's 2e-4 sits below this model's own fp32 noise floor at depth 36.
  **GPU encoder (fp16, unchanged kernels) en/cjk 0.024-0.027, empty 0.21**,
  and that number has a mechanism (`TestGPULadder`, kept as the permanent
  instrument): the residual stream grows a ~13k massive-activation channel
  at layer 6, carries it flat, and **cancels it in layers 34-35 — the two
  layers Z-Image never ran** — so the fp16 bulk-rounding variance the
  channel accumulated surfaces at the end (protecting just the spike
  elements measurably does not help). Priced against deployment: the
  **official bf16 pipeline deviates from fp32 by rel 2.0 (abs 204)** through
  the same mechanism — our fp16 path is 10-85x closer to fp32 than what the
  ecosystem ships. Not taken (priced): an fp32-activation GEMM arm for the
  encoder — at prompt-sized M (~40 rows) the encoder is weight-bandwidth-
  bound so it would be cheap; build it only if Q3/Q6 show prompt adherence
  suffering.
- **Q2 — one DiT block on CPU. Done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/dit`): layout
  (image ids/target mask/segments) **exact** vs the dump, RoPE tables at
  ~5e-7 (negative-index grids included), head pieces at ~1e-5, the no-block
  prefill/cached forwards at ~4e-6, and the block gate — out_prefill,
  cache K/V contents, out_cached, both cases — at **≤ 4e-5** against
  `out/qi21block`. The negative control (NeoX-halves rotary pairing) is
  caught at 1e5x the bound. `Load(dir, blocks)` takes 0/1/32 blocks, so Q3's
  stack is a loop away. One porting trap found and worth remembering:
  `chunk(2, -1)` splits *rows* — rewrapping the modulation's backing array
  at half width hands row 1 the second half of row 0, and every downstream
  tensor fails at rel ~10 while every shape checks out.
- **Q3 — the stack + scheduler + t2i sampler on CPU. Done 2026-09-20 at the
  latent gate** (`qimage/pipeline`): the dynamic-shift scheduler matches
  diffusers at ~1e-6 across all five dumped size/step cases (mu exact, the
  exponential shift, the terminal stretch, the Euler step), and
  `Denoise` — 32 blocks, ModeExtract at step 0 then cached decodes, exactly
  as served — reproduces the 256²/4-step oracle's **per-step latents at
  rel 2.1e-5 → 2.5e-4** (bound 1e-3, 4x measured; 2.3 min a sample on CPU).
  **Still owed to Q5**: the *image* gate — prompt → PNG with our own text
  encoder and VAE decode against the oracle's `image` tensor (Z-Image's
  2.2e-2 precedent). The three green gates (textenc, denoise, decoder) do
  not compose into that claim; it gets measured, once the decoder exists.
- **Q4 — DiT on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20 for t2i** (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`,
  ~750 lines on z-image's shader set): **1024²/40 steps in 90.7 s — prefill
  2.29 s, cached steps 2.27 s** — against CPU Go's ~2.5 h and torch fp32's
  ~35 min. The mapping that made it small: the block's LayerNorm+modulate+
  narrow is `dit_final_norm.comp` verbatim; the shared modulation is host
  arithmetic (ten uploaded vectors) with the t=0 row-select expressed as two
  dispatch ranges; SwiGLU's fp16 range problem is solved *exactly* by
  scaling 1/16 into fp16 and folding 16 into the uploaded tanh(gate) vector
  (2.1's down-proj feeds a gated residual, so z-image's norm-invariance
  trick was unavailable). Two new shaders: `dit_attn_causal.comp` (the
  prefill runs the WMMA kernel bidirectionally over the whole sequence and
  this recomputes the text rows' context causally — tens of rows, once per
  image) and `dit_copy.comp` (offset copies for the KV cache). The cache is
  each block's post-RoPE prefix k/v as fp32 arena rows, restored under the
  fresh target rows each step before a full re-pack (fine at t2i's tiny
  prefix; Q8's reference images want it fp16 + tile-masked, and the
  full-seq re-pack is a Q9 percent). **Gates, per
  `two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate`, both regimes against the oracle**:
  teacher-forced (each step fed the oracle's own latents — bounds the
  model) flat at 1.5e-3–8e-3 over all 40 steps at 1024², bound 2e-2;
  free-running drifts linearly at ~1.3e-3/step to 0.050 at 40 steps — a
  perturbed ODE diverging, the phenomenon diffusers documents for
  cache-on/off — bounded at 0.12 with the image judgment deferred to Q6's
  eyeball. Not done: tile re-screen at M=16384/K=12288 (running on
  z-image's measured winners uncontested — a Q9 percent), the VAE's GPU
  stage (with Q5's fp16-range constraint), and the negative-control
  breakages the z-image graph carries.
- **Q5 — the VAE in Go. CPU done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/vae`, on
  `zimage/vae`'s Tensor/Conv2D — whose Pad/PadEnd/Stride already carried the
  identical downsampler shape): decoder and encoder, stagewise against
  `out/qi21vae`, RGBA round trip included. The T=1 semantics are explicit in
  the package doc: causal 3D convs fold to 2D, time_convs never run,
  AvgDown3D *means in a zero frame* on temporal blocks, DupUp3D keeps only
  the last temporal copy. Two measured bounds: conv stages at 2e-4 (they run
  at ≤5e-5), and `normTol` 8e-3 for the stages where the model amplifies
  fp32 noise — the decoder past its per-pixel L2 tail norm (the dumped fp32
  reference is itself rel 1.3e-3 from a float64 decode there; our decoded
  image sits max abs 8.7e-4 from the dump, under a quarter of one 8-bit
  step) and the encoder's deep middle (the reference's own thread-order
  noise jumps 47x at down_blocks.3; we track ~5x that and land at 4.7e-5 on
  the posterior mode).
  **The end-to-end image gate Q3 owed is closed**: `TestEndToEndImage` runs
  prompt → image through our tokenizer, text encoder, DiT, scheduler and
  decoder — only the noise is the oracle's — and matches the 256²/4-step
  reference image at **max abs 9.1e-4, mean 6e-6** in [0, 1] space, 24x
  inside the 2.2e-2 precedent. (~65 GB fp32 passes through, sequenced to a
  ~34 GB peak; it must run alone.)
  **Still open in Q5: the GPU port**, which folds into Q4's GPU stage — and
  the fp16 constraint from Q0 stands: decoder intermediates reach absmax
  ~1e5–3e5 against fp16's 65504, so those stages need fp32 storage or a
  rescale, unlike z-image's decoder.
- **Q6 — serve t2i.** `-image` loads qimage; `/v1/images/generations` with
  geometry under a ceiling (multiples of 32 now, not 16), `background:
  "transparent"`, steps default 40. **First honest wall clock** (two runs) at
  1024² and 2048², and the **step-count sweep** (40/24/16/12, same seed,
  eyeball + a fixed prompt set) that decides the served default. Delete
  Z-Image weights and dead code after this lands.
- **Q7 — previews.** Fit the linear 64→RGB matrix from Q0's pairs, wire
  `stream: true`/`partial_images` back up.
- **Q8 — edits.** The big one, in three parts: (a) VAE encoder serving
  reference latents (Q5 built it), (b) **the vision tower** — 27-layer ViT,
  2x2 spatial merge, interpolated position grid, deepstack feature injection
  into the text model's first layers, mrope with real 3D positions — the
  largest genuinely new port in this migration, (c) multi-image template +
  per-ref RoPE blocks + prefix cache across refs. `/v1/images/edits` drops
  `strength`, gains multi-ref. Gate: edit dump match + an end-to-end edit vs
  the oracle.
- **Q9 — percents.** Only after capabilities: the I3/I5/I8/I9 fusion lesson
  (elementwise passes absorbed into consumers) transfers to a new but
  same-shaped budget; attribute before optimising, same-hour controls, plans

- **The cost profile inverts.** Z-Image-Turbo was an 8-step distillation;
  2.1 wants 40 steps. Estimates (labeled, not measured): Z-Image's DiT step at
  1024²/4096 tokens is ~1.5 s on this machine; 2.1's blocks carry ~1.13x the
  parameters ⇒ ~1.7 s/step ⇒ **~70 s per 1024² image (vs 14.3 s today)**, and
  2048² (GEMMs x4, attention x16) lands around **5–6 min**. Text encode
  (~0.5–2 s) and VAE decode (~1–2 s at 1024²) are noise against that. The two
  levers, in order: **the step count** (sweep 40/24/16/12 for quality — knob
  already exists) and **a distilled/turbo release or LoRA** (the ecosystem
  around it — lightx2v etc. — is where Z-Image-Turbo itself came from; watch
  for it). This is the price of the capability jump and the user accepted the
  rework knowing the model; still, **Q6's first measurement decides the served
  defaults**, and 1024²/40 is the starting point, not a commitment.

On 2026-09-20 the user decided to replace Z-Image-Turbo with
`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` (cloned at `models/Qwen-Image-2.1/`) for the whole
image vertical — generation *and* edits — accepting that the vertical breaks
during the rework. The plan lives in root `IMAGE.md` (stages Q0–Q9, decisions,
open questions Q-o1..Q-o5); the merged diffusers implementation is copied
verbatim into `reference/qwenimage21/` as the porting oracle.

**Why:** unified t2i + native multi-reference editing (up to 10 refs), native
RGBA, and a prefix-KV-cache architecture — a capability jump over Z-Image's
SDEdit-based edits, at the cost of 40 undistilled steps (~5x slower per image
until a turbo variant appears).

**How to apply:** read `IMAGE.md` before touching the image vertical; don't
resurrect z-image code paths. `zimage/qwen` and `zimage/tokenizer` survive
(shared by embed/llm/parakeet); new model code goes in a `qimage/` tree.
The dump env is the shared `.venv`: transformers 5.17.0 is fine (diffusers'
final-norm hook verified there, Q0), diffusers is pinned to git `80c7ed26`
(0.41.0.dev0 — stable 0.40.0 lacks the classes). The fp32 torch text-encoder
probes take ~34 GB and the full-pipeline oracle ~68 GB — **one at a time**:
on 2026-09-20 a 34 GB Go encoder test beside the running oracle got both
OOM-killed (the kernel picked the python at step 8 of 40). taehv's taew2_1 does
NOT fit this model's 64-channel/16x VAE — previews are a self-fitted linear
64→RGB matrix until upstream ships a real tiny decoder. See
[[docs-consolidated-into-research]], [[deployment-two-machines]].

`IMAGE.md` now records the day accurately. What changed:

- **The banner** no longer says "plan only — nothing is built"; it leads with the state: Q0–Q5 done for t2i (Q5's GPU stage excepted), CPU end-to-end matching diffusers below 8-bit quantization, and the GPU DiT at 2.27 s/step.
- **A "Where the work stands" table** (the house convention from the z-image vertical file) — one row per stage with its gate numbers, including the explicitly-named **Q5g** row: the VAE's GPU stage as the serving blocker between here and Q6.
- **The cost section** is converted from estimates to measurements: 90.7 s of transformer per 1024²/40-step image against the morning's ~70 s estimate, with the gap attributed (unported fusions, the full-seq re-pack — Q9), 2048² still marked as the one remaining estimate, and the step-count lever now priced in real seconds (~90 s vs ~27 s).
- **The "what survives" shaders row** upgraded from prediction to confirmation: the whole graph runs on z-image's kernels plus two small new shaders.
- **Q6's entry** now names its dependency on Q5g and inherits the free-run image eyeball that Q4's gate deferred.
- The banner also records the day's twice-used method finding: when a port exceeds a borrowed tolerance, measure the reference against itself before hunting a bug — three of the file's bounds were set that way.

The memory file got the same one-paragraph state update so future sessions recall where things stand before opening the plan.

One thing I deliberately didn't touch since you asked for IMAGE.md specifically: `TODO.md`'s image-vertical section still describes z-image at 14.3 s as the current state. Happy to rewrite that row to point at IMAGE.md whenever you want.
